# poo — Complete Documentation

Source: https://poo.douggo.com

---

<!-- Source: getting-started/why-poo.md -->

# Why poo?

Many JS-written harnesses like [pi](https://pi.dev) promote a *self-improving* agent. `poo` promotes an **engineered agent**.

Each approach fits different work. A self-improving harness fits when you want an agent that writes and loads its own extensions at runtime. `poo` fits when you want fixed capability boundaries, headless automation, or a custom Go binary.

From one Go codebase, `poo` ships two deliverables:

- A **headless CLI** (with an interactive [REPL](/getting-started/repl)) that runs sessions without a full terminal UI.
- An **embeddable Go library** that a wrapping application links into its own binary.

Unlinked packages cannot be reached at runtime. A read-only build omits `bash`, so no prompt or config can invoke a shell.

## The Extensibility Ladder

Not every customization requires writing Go. `poo` separates operational configuration from structural capability across three layers:

1. **Drop-in manifests (no rebuild):** Extend an existing `poo` binary with declarative JSON/YAML files on disk:
   - [`cli-registry`](/capabilities/cli-registry) manifests to expose CLI tools through `call_cli` (and `find_tool` when a catalog grows large).
   - [`mcp.json`](/capabilities/mcp-servers) manifests for MCP servers and resource feeds.
   - [`feeds`](/capabilities/feeds-and-daemon) manifests for long-lived command streams that deliver events into a session.
   - [`skills`](/capabilities/skills) directories (`SKILL.md`) for on-demand procedural guidance.
2. **YAML profiles & prompt sections (no rebuild):** Shape behavior per project or role in `settings.yaml`. Compose profiles (`base`, `code`, `search`, or custom profiles), append or swap named prompt sections, and tune compaction strategies. You can also attach permission rules, asker chains, and `bwrap` sandboxing.
3. **Compile-time Go binary (`server.New`):** Use this layer when you need hard capability boundaries, custom tools, custom executors, or a bespoke wire server. Import `poo` as a library, wire your packages into `server.New`, and ship a single static binary. See [Build Your Own Binary](/extending/custom-binary).

## Stdlib-Only Core

The core packages — `poo`, `poo/prompt`, `poo/decide`, and `poo/wire/protocol` — depend on the Go standard library only. `internal/depcheck` enforces this boundary in `go test`.

Opt-in packages (YAML/TOML config, MCP SDK, QuickJS/Starlark codemode, SQLite, readline) live outside the core. Consumers embedding `poo` only pull in the dependencies they actually link.

## Explicit FSM & Closed Settle Reasons

Agent loops built around `while True` and exception-driven control flow make wire protocols, session replay, and headless automation fragile. `poo` runs an explicit finite state machine:

```
idle → requesting → streaming → executing → compacting → settling → settled
```

Every run terminates with a closed, typed settle reason (such as completed, cancelled, turn/token/duration limit, or truncation). Runs never rely on a magic string printed to stdout or a control message mixed into the transcript. Tool calls are recorded as typed records with explicit outcomes, and the `finish` tool carries a schema-validated result.

## Non-Silent History

`poo` enforces a single governing rule for transcripts: **nothing rewrites the model's view of history silently.**

- The append-only session store preserves the full trajectory.
- Compaction never mutates or drops older turns behind the scenes. Strategies like `summary`, `handoff`, `mine`, `pointer`, and `native` record a visible, typed replacement in the session log while leaving the underlying store intact.
- The rendered system prompt is frozen for the length of a run so provider prompt caches remain valid.

## Proven on Evals

Architecture claims only matter if the harness can drive models through real multi-step engineering tasks. `poo` ships both a 20-task local evaluation suite (`poo-eval`) and a [Harbor](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor) adapter (`evals/harbor`) for Terminal-Bench and SWE-bench.

In head-to-head Terminal-Bench runs on locally hosted `glm-5.3-flash`, `poo` beat `pi` and tied `mini-swe-agent`. That is not an exhaustive benchmark across every frontier model, and results will vary by model and dataset. Still, it shows that `poo`'s explicit FSM, stateless shell contract, and compaction pipeline hold up under relentless autonomous runs.

## Further Reading

- [Prior Art](/extending/prior-art) — exactly what `poo` copies and rejects from `mini-swe-agent` and `pi-durable`.
- [Evals & Benchmarks](/reference/evals) — running `poo-eval` and the Harbor Terminal-Bench / SWE-bench adapter.
- [Build Your Own Binary](/extending/custom-binary) — wiring custom tools, profiles, and conformance tests at compile time.

<!-- Source: getting-started/install.md -->

# Install

`poo` ships as a single static binary for Linux and macOS (`amd64` and `arm64`).

## Release script (recommended)

Download the latest GitHub release binary, verify its SHA-256 checksum against `checksums.txt`, and install it to `~/.local/bin`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sdougbrown/poo/main/install.sh | sh
```

To install into a different directory, set `BINDIR`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sdougbrown/poo/main/install.sh | BINDIR=/usr/local/bin sh
```

If `BINDIR` is not on your `PATH`, the script prints the `export PATH=...` line to add to your shell profile.

## `go install`

Requires **Go 1.26 or newer**:

```bash
go install github.com/sdougbrown/poo/cmd/poo@latest
```

Pin a specific release tag by replacing `@latest` with `@vX.Y.Z`.

## Build from source

Development uses [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) to pin Go 1.26 (see `mise.toml`):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sdougbrown/poo.git
cd poo
mise install
mise exec -- go build -o poo ./cmd/poo
```

Run the vet and race-detector test suite to verify your checkout:

```bash
mise exec -- go vet ./...
mise exec -- go test -race ./...
```

## Verify the installation

`poo version` reports build information embedded in the binary. For a `go install ...@version` or release build, it shows the module version. For a checkout build, it shows the VCS revision, commit timestamp, and `modified` flag:

```bash
poo version
```

For scripts or CI pipelines that need to pin or inspect the binary, pass `--json`:

```bash
poo version --json
```

<!-- Source: getting-started/quickstart.md -->

# Quickstart

You can run a headless session in under a minute with either a local OpenAI-compatible server or a built-in cloud provider.

## Option A: Local OpenAI-compatible endpoint

No settings file is required. Pass `--endpoint` and `--model-id` directly to `poo run`:

```bash
poo run \
  --endpoint http://localhost:4000/v1 \
  --model-id gemma4 \
  --context-limit 262144 \
  --max-turns 8 \
  --log session.jsonl \
  "List the Go packages in this repository."
```

`poo` runs the session to completion, writes the structured transcript to `session.jsonl`, and exits with a code reflecting the settle reason.

## Option B: Built-in provider

`poo` ships built-in provider records for OpenCode Console, Codex (`openai-codex`), and Ollama Cloud. Authenticate once with `poo login`:

```bash
# Pick one:
poo login opencode
poo login codex
poo login ollama-cloud
```

Credentials are stored in `poo`'s default credential file (`~/.config/poo/auth.yaml` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/poo/auth.yaml` on macOS). Once authenticated, assign a model to the [`roles.chat` role](/configuration/models-and-catalog#roles-and-required-operations) in your settings file:

```yaml
# .poo/settings.yaml
version: 1
profile: code
roles:
  chat: opencode-go/glm-5.3        # or openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol, or ollama-cloud/glm-5.3
```

## Starter settings files

The repository includes annotated starter configs under `examples/`:

| File | Use case |
|---|---|
| `examples/code.settings.yaml` | Local OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`gemma4`), `code` profile, `decide` asker, `bwrap` executor, `summary` compaction. |
| `examples/sandboxed.settings.yaml` | `code` profile with guardrails: `unmatched: ask`, `bwrap` with `network: false`, `protected_paths`, `restrict_to_working_dir`, and `fetch` disabled. |
| `examples/opencode.settings.yaml` | OpenCode Console gateway (`opencode-go/glm-5.3`), no `endpoints` or `models` block needed. |
| `examples/codex.settings.yaml` | Built-in `openai-codex` provider with `native` compaction and model-family prompt guidance. |

Copy one to `.poo/settings.yaml` in your project root (or `~/.config/poo/settings.yaml` as your user default), or pass it explicitly with `--settings`:

```bash
poo run --settings examples/code.settings.yaml "Run go test ./... and summarize any failures."
```

## Preflight with `poo roles`

Before starting a session, verify that every [role](/configuration/models-and-catalog#roles-and-required-operations) in your settings resolves to a valid model and credential:

```bash
poo roles
```

`poo roles` prints each assigned role, the provider serving it, and where that provider's credential comes from — without printing secrets or making network calls. If a role cannot resolve, it exits non-zero and lists the models that could serve it.

## Launch the interactive REPL

With a settings file in place, run a bare `poo` to open the interactive REPL:

```bash
poo
```

`poo` discovers settings automatically in order: `--settings`, `POO_SETTINGS`, `.poo/settings.{json,yaml,yml,toml}` walking up from the current directory, then your user config directory. See [Interactive REPL](/getting-started/repl) for slash commands and keybindings.

## Next Steps

- **Tune reasoning effort and sampling** for custom or local models: [Reasoning & Sampling](/configuration/reasoning-and-sampling)
- **Run async event feeds in a resident daemon**: [Feeds & Daemon](/capabilities/feeds-and-daemon)
- **Add a CLI tool without rebuilding `poo`**: [CLI Registry & Script Tools](/capabilities/cli-registry)
- **Lock down bash and filesystem access**: [Sandboxing (`bwrap`)](/operations/sandbox)

<!-- Source: getting-started/repl.md -->

# Interactive REPL

`poo repl` is poo's terminal interface. It accepts the same flags as `poo serve`, launches `poo serve` as a subprocess, and connects to it over the JSON-RPC wire protocol. Replies render as Markdown with syntax-highlighted code blocks, and tool calls and results render as decorated blocks.

## Starting the REPL

```bash
# Launch the default UI (repl)
poo

# Explicit subcommand with flags
poo repl --profile code --working-dir ./my-repo
```

Running bare `poo` launches the interface configured by `ui` in settings (defaulting to `repl`). If no settings file exists yet, bare `poo` runs an interactive setup flow in the terminal to configure a sign-in and chat model.

To use a different default profile in interactive sessions than in headless `poo run` / `poo serve` invocations, set `repl_profile` in your settings file.

When stdin and stdout are both terminals, the REPL pins the input editor and statusline to the bottom. The transcript scrolls above them. When piped, it falls back to plain line-oriented I/O.

## Input Editing and Keybindings

At a terminal, the REPL uses a readline editor in **vi insert mode** (`vi-insert`) and persists input history in `<user-cache-dir>/poo/repl-history-v2`.

### Control Keys and Bash Chords

| Key | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `Enter` | Submit the entire draft (including multi-line drafts). |
| `Ctrl-J` | Insert a newline into the draft without submitting. |
| `Esc` | Stop the active turn/run if working; switch to vi command mode (`vi-command`) when idle. |
| `Ctrl-C` | Cancel the active run if working; clear the current draft if non-empty; exit the REPL (exit code `130`) when the prompt is empty. |
| `Shift+Tab` | Cycle the chat model's reasoning level (same as `/thinking`). |
| `Ctrl-A` | Jump to the beginning of the line. |
| `Ctrl-E` | Jump to the end of the line. |
| `Ctrl-B` | Move cursor back one character. |
| `Ctrl-F` | Move cursor forward one character. |
| `Ctrl-T` | Transpose the two characters before the cursor. |
| `Ctrl-K` | Kill from the cursor to the end of the line. |
| `Ctrl-U` | Clear from the cursor to the start of the line. |
| `Ctrl-W` | Cut the word behind the cursor. |

### Steering an Active Run

Submitting a regular message (not a slash command) during an active run sends a **steer** message (`run/message`). The session queues it and delivers it to the model at the end of the current turn. Slash commands other than `/bg` wait until the run settles.

## Slash Commands

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `/model` | List available models in the catalog (numbered), marking the active chat model with `←`. |
| `/model <text>` | Switch to an exact model name, or filter the catalog by fragment. A single match switches immediately; multiple matches print a ranked, numbered list. |
| `/model <number>` | Switch to a model by number from the most recent `/model` or `/models` list. |
| `/models` | Probe configured endpoints for what they currently serve, refresh the catalog, and list the models. Supports `/models <text>` and `/models <number>`. |
| `/thinking` | Cycle the reasoning level (`default`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `off`). Same as `Shift+Tab`. |
| `/thinking <level>` | Set the reasoning level explicitly, or pass a token budget for budget-based models. `default` omits the reasoning field; `off` asks the model not to think. |
| `/bg` | Move the currently running backgroundable tool call (such as `bash`) into a session background job without restarting it. |
| `/less` | Open the session transcript in `less -R`. |
| `/help` | Show the command list (aliases: `/h`, `?`). |
| `/cancel` | Cancel the active run. |
| `/quit` | Close the session and exit the REPL (aliases: `/q`, `/exit`). |

::: tip Backgrounding with `/bg`
`/bg` only moves a call when exactly one backgroundable call is running. The promoted job survives run cancellation, but it keeps the original `bash` command timeout. For long-running work that needs the full job timeout, instruct the model to run it in the background from the start (so it launches with `background: true`).
:::

## Permission Prompts

The REPL declares the `permission_answers` wire capability, so asks routed to the `wire` asker appear inline in the terminal:

```text
⚙ permission · bash
rm -rf build/
  allow bash? [y/N]
```

Type `y` or `yes` to allow the call. Any other input — including pressing `Enter` on an empty line or reaching EOF — denies the call. See [Permissions & Safety](/operations/permissions-and-safety) for configuring rules and askers.

## Statusline

The statusline sits on the bottom row of the pinned footer (or inline before the prompt when no pinned footer is active) and displays:

```text
⌂ my-repo │ ⎇ main │ gpt-6 │ 🧠 medium │ ctx 12.4k/128k
```

- **Folder (`⌂`)** — basename of the session's working directory.
- **Git branch (`⎇`)** — current branch or short commit hash when in a detached HEAD (omitted outside a git repository).
- **Model** — active chat model name.
- **Reasoning (`🧠`)** — active reasoning level (omitted when set to `default`).
- **Context fill (`ctx`)** — input token count from the most recent request against the model's prompt limit.

## Continuing and Resuming Sessions

Logged sessions can be reopened directly from the command line:

```bash
# Reopen the most recently active unlocked session for the current directory
poo repl --continue
poo repl -c
poo -c

# Reopen a specific session by ID
poo repl --resume <session-id>
poo --resume <session-id>
```

Find session IDs with `poo sessions list`.

When a session is reopened:

- It retains the working directory, profile, and model recorded in its log.
- The REPL renders up to the **newest 500 history items** as scrollback before the first prompt. None of the replayed scrollback is re-sent to the model.
- If the previous process crashed, any recovery actions (such as a truncated tail or interrupted runs) are shown as a warning.
- `--continue` skips sessions currently locked by another process.

### Refusals (Exit Code 2)

The REPL refuses to start and exits with code `2` when:

- Both `--continue` and `--resume` are passed together.
- `--continue` finds no unlocked logged session matching the working directory.
- `--ephemeral` or `session.mode: ephemeral` is active.
- `--resume <id>` targets a session whose recorded working directory differs from the current one (resume from that directory or pass `--working-dir <dir>`).

<!-- Source: configuration/settings-discovery.md -->

# Settings Discovery

Every poo command loads a single settings file—there is no merging across project and user settings files. If discovery finds no file, poo runs on defaults that CLI flags can override.

For the full list of supported keys, see the [Settings Reference](/reference/settings).

## Discovery Order

Commands check these locations in order and stop at the first match:

1. **CLI flag (`--settings <path>`)**: Uses the exact path given. If the file does not exist, poo fails immediately.
2. **Environment variable (`POO_SETTINGS`)**: Uses the exact path in `POO_SETTINGS`. If the file does not exist, poo fails immediately.
3. **Project directory (`.poo/`)**: Starts in the working directory (or current directory when empty) and walks up to the filesystem root, checking `<dir>/.poo/` at each level.
4. **User config directories**:
   - **Linux**: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/poo` when set, otherwise `~/.config/poo`.
   - **macOS**: `~/Library/Application Support/poo` first, then `~/.config/poo`.
   - **Windows**: `%AppData%\poo`.

::: tip Explicit paths are promises
Missing files in `.poo/` or user config directories are skipped silently. A missing path passed via `--settings` or `POO_SETTINGS` always fails the command.
:::

## File Extension Priority & Formats

Inside each searched directory, poo looks for these filenames in order:

1. `settings.json`
2. `settings.yaml`
3. `settings.yml`
4. `settings.toml`

The first regular file found wins. A `settings.json` in the same directory shadows `settings.yaml`, `settings.yml`, and `settings.toml`.

The file extension selects the parser:

| Extension | Parser |
|---|---|
| `.yaml`, `.yml` | YAML |
| `.toml` | TOML |
| `.json` (or any other / no extension) | JSON |

All three formats normalize to the same canonical JSON representation before decoding, so keys, types, and validation rules behave identically across JSON, YAML, and TOML.

## Strict Unknown-Key Rejection

Settings are decoded strictly (`DisallowUnknownFields`). Any unrecognized key—or a key with the wrong value type—fails the load and names the offending field.

Validation runs in two stages after decoding:

1. **Schema rules** (`config/schema/settings.umpire.json`): Enforces required fields (`version: 1`), value ranges and enums, mutual exclusions (such as `skills.default` vs `skills.user_path`, and `system_prompt.base_file` vs `system_prompt.replace`), and cross-field dependencies (such as `permission.decide.*` requiring `roles.decider`).
2. **Runtime checks**: Validates role names, permission rule structure, asker names, protected path globs, engine-specific limits, and the existence of referenced files (`system_prompt.base_file`, `finish.schema_file`, `session.user_prompt_file`, `pi_auth_file`).

### Legacy Key Aliases

Three pre-v1 keys are still accepted and rewritten automatically when the current key name is absent:

| Legacy key | Current key | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| `cliregistry` | `cli_registry` | Any depth |
| `pi_models_file` | `models_file` | Any depth |
| `base_url` | `endpoint` | Entries inside `endpoints` only |

## Relative Path Resolution Rules

Absolute paths are always kept as-is. Leading `~` or `~/` expands to the current user's home directory (`$HOME`) across all path keys (`~user` is not expanded and is treated as a relative path).

Relative paths resolve against different base directories depending on the key:

### Resolved against the settings file's directory

These keys point to companion configuration files that travel with the settings file:

- `models_file`
- `auth_file`
- `pi_auth_file`
- `profiles_files`
- `system_prompt.base_file`
- `finish.schema_file`
- `profiles.<name>.prompt_file` (when declared inline in the settings file)
- `profiles.<name>.prompt_append_file` (when declared inline in the settings file)

When `config.Parse` parses a settings document in memory with no file path, relative paths in these keys stay relative to the working directory.

### Resolved against the declaring profiles file's directory

When a profile loads from an external file in `profiles_files`, these keys resolve against **that profiles file's directory** rather than the main settings directory:

- `profiles.<name>.prompt_file`
- `profiles.<name>.prompt_append_file`

### Resolved against the working directory

These keys point to project-scoped manifests and guidance directories:

- `cli_registry.paths`
- `feeds.paths`
- `mcp.paths`
- `skills.paths`

Leading `~` or `~/` in any of these lists resolves under the user's home directory instead of the working directory.

### Home expansion only (relative to process working directory)

These keys expand a leading `~` or `~/` and otherwise pass through relative to the process working directory:

- `session.dir` (defaults to `~/.local/state/poo/sessions`)
- `session.user_prompt_file`
- `skills.user_path`

### Default Companion File Discovery

When optional companion keys are omitted, poo checks beside the settings file or in the platform user config directory:

| Resource | Default behavior when omitted |
|---|---|
| `models_file` | Loads `models.yaml` or `models.json` beside the settings file (having both in the same directory is an error). |
| `auth_file` / `pi_auth_file` | Uses `auth.yaml` or `auth.json` beside the loaded `models_file`, or `auth.yaml` (falling back to legacy `auth.json`) in the user config directory. On macOS, an existing `~/.config/poo/auth.yaml` (or `auth.json`) stands in when the native `~/Library/Application Support/poo/` file is absent. |
| `cli_registry.defaults`, `feeds.defaults`, `mcp.defaults` | Enabled (`true`) by default; loads `cli-registry/`, `feeds/`, and `mcp/` from the user config directory (with `~/.config/poo/` fallback on macOS). |
| `session.user_prompt` | Reads `AGENTS.md` from the native user config directory (`~/Library/Application Support/poo` on macOS). |

---

<!-- Source: configuration/models-and-catalog.md -->

# Models & Catalog

poo resolves every model through a single catalog that merges built-in family rules, live endpoint discovery, a models file, and `settings.yaml`. Sessions and transports read the merged `ModelInfo` record from this catalog.

## Endpoints, Models, and Roles

Configuration splits model setup into three blocks in `settings.yaml` (see [Settings Reference](/reference/settings)):

- **`endpoints`** — where a server lives and how to reach it (`endpoint` base URL, `api_key_env` or `api_key`, optional `session_header`, `skip_probe`, `instructions_per_question`).
- **`models`** — named model declarations that pair an endpoint name with a `model_id` and any model-specific overrides (`api`, `context_limit`, `input_limit`, `max_output`, `inputs`, `ops`, `tools_mode`, `reasoning`, `reasoning_levels`, `quirks`, `prompt_variant`).
- **`roles`** — assigns a catalog model name to each job a session performs.

```yaml
version: 1

endpoints:
  local:
    endpoint: http://localhost:4000/v1
    api_key_env: LOCAL_API_KEY

models:
  coder:
    endpoint: local
    model_id: qwen3-coder-30b
    context_limit: 131072
    max_output: 16384
    tools_mode: native

roles:
  chat: coder
  compaction: local/qwen3-8b
```

A role can reference a model declared under `models` (`coder`) or a model provided by a models file or live discovery using its `<endpoint>/<id>` name (`local/qwen3-8b`).

### Roles and Required Operations

| Role | Purpose | Required `ops` | Required? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `chat` | Primary conversation and tool-calling turns | `chat` | Yes (session fails to build if unresolved) |
| `decider` | Fast yes/no permission and state decisions (see [Decision Model](/capabilities/decision-model)) | `systemone` or `decisions` | Optional (warning if unresolved) |
| `compaction` | Summarizing or reconstructing history during compaction (see [Context Compaction](/capabilities/compaction)) | `chat` | Optional (warning if unresolved) |

If no layer sets `ops` on a model, the catalog defaults it to `[chat]`. Assigning a model that does not declare the operation a role needs (for example, assigning a `systemone`-only decider model to `chat`) is a configuration error.

## Catalog Layering

Each model in the catalog is assembled from four layers merged in order. Later layers win **field by field** — setting one field in a higher layer leaves every other field from lower layers intact:

1. **`curated`** — family rules embedded in the binary (`gemma`, `qwen`, `minimax`), matched by `model_id` prefix. They supply family defaults such as `context_limit`, `ops`, `tools.mode`, `reasoning`, `temperature`, and `prompt_cache`.
2. **`discovery`** — what the endpoint reports when probed (OpenAI `/models`, llama.cpp server props, or Ollama model show). Results are cached at `<StateDir>/poo/discovery.json` with a 10-minute freshness TTL (`DefaultDiscoveryTTL`). Session builds read the local cache without blocking on network probes; `poo models` and `poo models --explain` reprobe live. Set `skip_probe: true` on endpoints that do not expose a model list.
3. **`models_file`** — endpoints and models declared in a models file, assembled in two steps:
   - First, the embedded `builtin-models.yaml` (or the file named by `POO_BUILTIN_MODELS`) when a credential file exists, gated to endpoints whose credentials are present.
   - Second, your `models.yaml` or imported pi `models.json` (set via `models_file` or auto-discovered beside `settings.yaml`), folded over the built-ins by name.
4. **`settings`** — `endpoints`, `models`, and top-level `sampling` in `settings.yaml`.

Any field still unset after all four layers takes a catalog default (`default` layer): `api` defaults to the endpoint's `api` or `chat_completions`, and `ops` defaults to `[chat]`.

For the full `models.yaml` schema, pi `models.json` import rules, and `POO_BUILTIN_MODELS` behavior, see [Models File Reference](/reference/models-file). For credential resolution and built-in providers, see [Providers & Auth](/configuration/providers-and-auth).

## Context, Input, and Output Limits

poo distinguishes three token limits on a model:

| Field | Meaning | Effect |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `context_limit` | Total context window shared by prompt and response | Sizes the output room (`max_tokens`) and bounds prompt size when `input_limit` is unset |
| `input_limit` | Largest prompt the endpoint accepts (when smaller than `context_limit`) | Caps the prompt budget used by compaction and model-switch checks (`min(context_limit, input_limit)`), while leaving `max_tokens` sized from `context_limit` |
| `max_output` | Maximum tokens the model writes in one response | Sets the request's `max_tokens` ceiling |

poo always computes and sends `max_tokens` rather than relying on an endpoint's hidden default. When `max_output` is unset or `0`, poo derives a default ceiling from `context_limit`:

| `context_limit` | Default `max_output` |
| :--- | :--- |
| Unknown (`<= 0`) | `16384` |
| `< 65536` | `8192` |
| `65536` – `131071` | `16384` |
| `>= 131072` | `32768` |

Before sending a request, poo clamps `max_tokens` to the room remaining in `context_limit` after the estimated prompt and output reserve (floored at `1`).

## Inspecting the Catalog

### `poo models` and `poo models --explain`

Run `poo models` to reprobe configured endpoints and print every available model:

```bash
poo models
poo models --json
```

To see every resolved field for one model and **which layer set it**, pass `--explain`:

```bash
poo models --explain coder
poo models --explain openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol
```

Output shows `FIELD`, `VALUE`, and `LAYER` (`curated`, `discovery`, `models_file`, `settings`, or `default`), including nested fields such as `reasoning.mode`, `reasoning.param`, `reasoning.levels`, `tools.mode`, and `sampling.temperature`. Use this whenever a model behaves unexpectedly to see whether a value came from family defaults, a probe, a models file, or `settings.yaml`.

### `poo roles`

Run `poo roles` to verify role resolution before starting a session:

```bash
poo roles
```

It prints a table of `ROLE`, `MODEL`, `PROVIDER`, and `CREDENTIAL` (`env:<VAR>`, `static`, or `none`) for `chat`, `decider`, and `compaction`:

- Prints no secrets and triggers no token refresh.
- Uses the same catalog resolution as a session build.
- Exits non-zero if any assigned role cannot be resolved or does not serve the required operation. In that case, it lists the catalog models that could serve that role.

---

<!-- Source: configuration/reasoning-and-sampling.md -->

# Reasoning & Sampling

poo separates **how a model controls reasoning** from **what reasoning level a session requests**. You declare the control mechanism on the model definition, and set the requested level in `reasoning.chat`, CLI flags, or the REPL.

## Setting Reasoning Effort on a Custom Model

A common mistake with custom models is setting `reasoning.chat: medium` without telling poo how the model accepts reasoning on the wire. Without a `reasoning` control on the model definition, poo treats the model as `mode: none` and refuses the setting with a configuration error.

Setting reasoning effort on a custom model takes **two parts**:

1. **Declare the model's reasoning control** on the model entry in `settings.yaml` (or [models.yaml](/reference/models-file)).
2. **Select the active level** in `settings.yaml`, via `--reasoning-effort`, or interactively in the REPL.

```yaml
# settings.yaml
version: 1

endpoints:
  myserver:
    endpoint: https://api.example.com/v1
    api_key_env: EXAMPLE_API_KEY

models:
  custom-reasoner:
    endpoint: myserver
    model_id: my-reasoning-model
    context_limit: 131072
    # Part 1: declare how this model accepts reasoning
    reasoning:
      mode: effort
      param: reasoning_effort
    # Optional: restrict accepted levels (lowest first)
    reasoning_levels: [off, low, medium, high]

roles:
  chat: custom-reasoner

# Part 2: select the active reasoning level
reasoning:
  chat: medium
```

You can also set Part 2 per run or interactively:

- **CLI (`poo run`)**: `--reasoning-effort medium`. When you pass a named effort level (`minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`) on `--reasoning-effort`, `poo run` forces `reasoning: { mode: effort, param: reasoning_effort }` even if the model did not declare one. Passing `default` or `off` preserves the model's own reasoning control.
- **REPL**: press `Shift+Tab` or run `/thinking` to cycle levels, or run `/thinking medium` (or `/thinking <tokens>` for budget models). See [Interactive REPL](/getting-started/repl).

Verify the merged control on any model with `poo models --explain <model>`.

## Reasoning Modes

`reasoning.mode` declares how a model's thinking is controlled on the wire. Four modes exist:

| Mode | Purpose | Default `param` if omitted |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `none` | Model reasoning cannot be controlled (default when unset) | — |
| `toggle` | Boolean on/off switch (common on local servers) | `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking` |
| `effort` | Named effort level (`minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, or model-declared levels) | `reasoning_effort` |
| `budget` | Positive integer token budget | `thinking.budget_tokens` |

### How Settings Map to Request Fields

The table below shows what poo sends for each combination of `reasoning.chat` (or session level) and `reasoning.mode`:

| Setting | `none` | `toggle` | `effort` | `budget` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `default` (or unset) | No field | No field | No field | No field |
| `off` | No field | `<param>: false` | Off word or quietest level (see below) | No field |
| Named level (e.g. `high`) | Error | `<param>: true` | `<param>: "<level>"` | Error |
| Positive integer (e.g. `4096`) | Error | `<param>: true` | Error | `<param>: 4096` |

- `default` always omits the reasoning field so the endpoint's own default applies.
- `off` is accepted by every model: `toggle` sends `false`, `effort` sends the model's off word (or quietest level), and `none`/`budget` omit the field.

### Common `param` Spellings

`reasoning.param` supports dot-separated paths, which poo encodes as nested JSON objects in the request body:

| Backend / API | `mode` | `param` | Wire JSON sent |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions | `effort` | `reasoning_effort` | `{"reasoning_effort": "medium"}` |
| OpenAI Responses / Codex (`api: responses`) | `effort` | `reasoning_effort` | `{"reasoning": {"effort": "medium", "summary": "auto"}}` |
| Local servers (llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang) | `toggle` | `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking` | `{"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": true}}` |
| Anthropic Messages (adaptive effort) | `effort` | `output_config.effort` | `{"output_config": {"effort": "high"}, "thinking": {"type": "adaptive"}}` |
| Anthropic Messages (token budget) | `budget` | `thinking.budget_tokens` | `{"thinking": {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 4096}}` |

Notes on transport behavior:
- **Anthropic Messages (`api: anthropic_messages`)**: when `param` starts with `output_config.`, the transport automatically sets `thinking.type: "adaptive"`. When `param` starts with `thinking.`, it automatically sets `thinking.type: "enabled"`.
- **Codex / Responses (`api: responses`)**: only accepts `mode: effort` with `param: reasoning_effort`. Toggle or budget controls on a Responses model return a configuration error.

## `reasoning_levels` and Off-Word Handling

`reasoning_levels` lists the exact levels a model accepts, ordered **lowest first**:

```yaml
reasoning:
  mode: effort
  param: reasoning_effort
reasoning_levels: [none, low, medium, high, xhigh]
```

When `reasoning_levels` is set:

- **Validation**: poo rejects levels outside the list (except `default` and `off`) instead of sending a value the server would ignore or reject.
- **Verbatim spelling**: declared levels are sent as spelled (including custom names such as `max` or `none`).
- **REPL cycling**: `/thinking` and `Shift+Tab` cycle through the model's declared levels.
- **`off` resolution on `effort` models**:
  1. If `reasoning_levels` contains `"off"` or `"none"`, poo sends that word verbatim (so an endpoint that spells off as `none` receives `"none"`).
  2. If `reasoning_levels` is non-empty but contains neither `"off"` nor `"none"`, poo sends the first (quietest) declared level (e.g. `"low"`).
  3. If `reasoning_levels` is empty, poo sends `"none"`.
  4. On the Codex Responses transport, `off` is always translated to `reasoning.effort: "none"`.

When switching models mid-session in the REPL, if the current reasoning level is not accepted by the new model, poo resets it to `off`.

## Per-Model Sampling

poo supports four sampling parameters: `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, and `min_p`. Unset parameters are omitted from requests so the endpoint uses its own defaults.

Sampling is layered in two places:

1. **Model defaults** in [models.yaml](/reference/models-file) under `endpoints.<ep>.models.<id>.sampling`.
2. **Per-model overrides** in `settings.yaml` under the top-level `sampling` map, keyed by catalog model name:

```yaml
# settings.yaml
sampling:
  local/qwen3-coder:
    temperature: 0.2
    top_p: 0.9
    top_k: 40
    min_p: 0.05
```

Overrides merge field by field over the model's defaults.

- If a model's catalog temperature mode is `fixed` or `unsupported`, poo drops `temperature` even when an override sets it.
- The Anthropic Messages transport sends `temperature`, `top_p`, and `top_k` (it does not send `min_p`).

## Transport Quirks

`quirks` is an ordered list of named request-shaping and response-repair adaptations applied by the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions transport. Set `quirks` on a model in `settings.yaml` or `models.yaml`:

```yaml
models:
  local-audio:
    endpoint: sglang
    model_id: qwen-omni
    inputs: [text, audio]
    quirks: [think_tags, audio_url]
```

Shipped quirks:

| Quirk | Phase | Behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `think_tags` | Response | Extracts `<think>...</think>` blocks from streamed text into structured thinking blocks |
| `chat_template_thinking` | Request | Sets `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking: true` unless already claimed by the model's reasoning control |
| `simplify_tool_schemas` | Request | Strips tool parameter JSON schemas down to `type`, `properties`, and `required` for servers with weak schema parsers |
| `degenerate_stream` | Response | Detects and logs repetitive/degenerate output loops without interrupting the stream |
| `text_tool_calls` | Response | Enables the text tool-call parser even when `tools_mode` is not `text` or `auto` |
| `audio_url` | Request | Rewrites `input_audio` content parts to `audio_url` data URLs (needed by servers such as SGLang that mirror `image_url`) |

Rules:
- Quirks run in the order listed.
- A quirk never overrides a request parameter already set by the model's `reasoning` or `sampling` controls.
- Unknown quirk names are skipped with a warning rather than failing the request.

## Tool-Calling Modes (`tools_mode`)

`tools_mode` controls how poo advertises tools and parses tool calls for a model:

| Value | Behavior |
| :--- | :--- |
| `native` | Sends tool definitions on the wire and reads structured wire tool calls |
| `text` | Describes tools in the system prompt and parses tool calls from response text |
| `auto` | Sends tool definitions on the wire and falls back to parsing response text when the wire returns no tool calls |
| `none` | Sends no tools |

When `tools_mode` is `text` or `auto`, the OpenAI Chat Completions text parser supports `hermes`, `qwen_xml`, `mistral`, `json`, and `auto` formats (set by the curated catalog's `tools.text_format`, defaulting to `auto`). On the Anthropic Messages transport, `native`, `auto`, and unset all send native wire tools.

---

<!-- Source: configuration/providers-and-auth.md -->

# Providers & Auth

`poo` separates **credentials** (OAuth tokens and API keys) from **endpoints** (URLs, wire APIs, and headers). Built-in providers activate automatically when a credential is available, and custom endpoints can speak OpenAI Chat Completions or Anthropic Messages.

## Credential Files & Resolution

### File Formats

`poo` reads three credential file shapes and preserves the format it reads when writing back:

1. **`poo` versioned format (`auth.yaml`, default)** — YAML with a top-level `version: 1` and a `credentials` map. OAuth entries use the same field names as `pi`:
   ```yaml
   version: 1
   credentials:
     openai-codex:
       type: oauth
       access: ...
       refresh: ...
       expires: 1767225600000
       accountId: ...
   ```
   A JSON file in this same versioned shape is read as the same document and written as YAML on the first write.
2. **Legacy `auth.json` and `pi`'s `auth.json`** — Unversioned JSON keyed directly by provider ID. An existing `auth.json` in `poo`'s config directory is read in place so prior sign-ins are not lost; renaming it to `auth.yaml` moves `poo` with it. When `pi_auth_file` points at `pi`'s `auth.json`, `poo` preserves `pi`'s JSON shape so `pi` can keep reading it.
3. **Codex CLI `auth.json` (read-only)** — Owned and refreshed by the Codex CLI. `poo` reads the access token's `exp` claim and never writes to the file (requires `auth_readonly: true`).

### Path Resolution & Platform Defaults

Configure the credential path in settings with either `auth_file` or `pi_auth_file` (setting both is rejected):

```yaml
# Keep credentials beside your settings file
auth_file: auth.yaml
```

Relative paths resolve against the settings file's directory. When using `auth_file`, pass the same `--settings` path to `poo login`, `poo auth status`, and `poo auth refresh`.

When neither `auth_file` nor `pi_auth_file` is set, `poo` resolves the credential file in this order:

1. **Beside a loaded models file** — If a `models_file` (or adjacent `models.yaml` / `models.json`) is loaded, `poo` looks beside it for `auth.yaml`, `auth.json`, or `pi`'s `auth.json` (beside `models.json`).
2. **Platform config directory**:
   - **macOS**: `~/Library/Application Support/poo/auth.yaml`. If absent, `poo` falls back to an existing `~/.config/poo/auth.yaml` without merging the two. If neither exists, `poo login` creates the native `Application Support` file.
   - **Linux & Windows**: `auth.yaml` in `poo`'s platform config directory (e.g. `~/.config/poo/auth.yaml` on Linux).

### Credential Precedence

For API-key endpoints, `poo` resolves keys in strict order:

1. **Environment variable** named by the endpoint's `api_key_env` (highest precedence).
2. **Credential file** key entry matching that provider's environment variable (for example, an endpoint declaring `api_key_env: OLLAMA_API_KEY` reads the `ollama-cloud` key stored via `poo login ollama-cloud`).
3. **Literal `api_key`** written in settings or a models file (lowest precedence).

### Read-Only Mode (`auth_readonly`)

Set `auth_readonly: true` when sharing a credential file managed by another tool:

```yaml
auth_file: ~/.codex/auth.json
auth_readonly: true
```

In read-only mode, `poo` never writes to the file: `poo login`, `poo auth import`, `poo auth refresh`, and token refreshes during sessions are all refused. If the access token expires, `poo` returns an error directing you to refresh with the owning tool.

## Built-in Providers

Built-in provider definitions ship in `builtin-models.yaml` (override the embedded file with `POO_BUILTIN_MODELS=/path/to/file.yaml`). A built-in provider's models appear in the catalog once a credential for it is in reach. Models declared in `models_file` or settings `models` always win on name collisions. See [Models & Catalog](/configuration/models-and-catalog) for layering details.

| Provider | Sign-in command | Auth method / Env var | Wire API | Probed |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `openai-codex` | `poo login codex` | OAuth (`chatgpt.com/backend-api`) | `responses` | No |
| `ollama-cloud` | `poo login ollama-cloud` | Key / `OLLAMA_API_KEY` | `chat_completions` | Yes |
| `opencode` / `opencode-go` | `poo login opencode` | Key / `OPENCODE_API_KEY` | `chat_completions` | Yes |
| `opencode-anthropic` / `opencode-go-anthropic` | `poo login opencode` | Key / `OPENCODE_API_KEY` | `anthropic_messages` | Yes |
| `typesafe` | `poo login typesafe` | Key / `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` | Decisions (`ops: [systemone]`) | No |

::: tip Key input security
Key-based `poo login <provider>` flows prompt interactively (with hidden input) or read a single line from `stdin`. There is no `--key` flag, keeping secrets out of shell history and process lists.
:::

### OpenAI Codex (`openai-codex`)

`openai-codex` uses OAuth against `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api` with `api: responses` and `skip_probe: true`. `poo` pins the OAuth credential strictly to that endpoint and refuses to send it anywhere else. Codex models serve `chat` turns and cannot be assigned to `decider`.

```yaml
roles:
  chat: openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol
```

**Sign in:**

```sh
poo login codex
```

`poo login codex` (or `poo login openai-codex`) opens your browser and listens on a loopback callback port (default timeout: 5 minutes, adjustable with `--wait <seconds>`). Pass `--force` to replace an existing credential without prompting.

For headless or remote machines, use `--no-browser`:

```sh
poo login codex --no-browser
```

Open the printed URL on a machine with a browser, then paste the full final redirect URL back into the terminal (including its `state` query parameter; a bare authorization code is rejected).

**Background token refresh (`poo auth refresh`):**

`poo auth refresh` checks the same credential file that sessions use and refreshes `openai-codex` when the access token has 5 minutes or less remaining. It prints nothing on success, exits non-zero on failure, and makes no model request.

```sh
poo auth refresh --settings /abs/path/to/settings.yaml --leeway 30m
```

- Use `--leeway <duration>` (e.g. `30m`) to refresh earlier.
- Use `--force` for manual one-off refreshes regardless of expiry.
- For idle or daemonized agents, run `poo auth refresh` from a `systemd` user timer or `launchd` job with an absolute `--settings` path. Schedule the timer more frequently than `--leeway`, and **do not** pass `--force` on a timer. If OpenAI revokes the refresh grant, you must run `poo login codex` again.

**Importing from `pi` (`poo auth import pi`):**

```sh
poo auth import pi [--from /path/to/auth.json] [--force]
```

Copies the `openai-codex` OAuth credential from `--from`, then `pi_auth_file`, then `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` into `poo`'s credential file without modifying `pi`'s file.

::: warning One-way door
OAuth refreshes rotate the refresh token, so only one tool can own a grant's refresh lifecycle. After `poo`'s first refresh, `pi`'s copy becomes stale; if `pi` refreshes first, `poo`'s copy stops working. Run one tool per grant, not both.
:::

**Sharing Codex CLI's credential:**

To reuse a sign-in owned by the Codex CLI without conflicting refreshes, point `auth_file` at `~/.codex/auth.json` and enable `auth_readonly: true`. Run the Codex CLI to refresh when expired.

### Ollama Cloud (`ollama-cloud`)

```sh
poo login ollama-cloud
```

Stores an API key for `https://ollama.com/v1` (also reachable via `OLLAMA_API_KEY`). `poo` probes the endpoint immediately after login so the live model list is ready for your first session, and refreshes it on `poo models` or `/models`. Reference models as `ollama-cloud/<id>`:

```yaml
roles:
  chat: ollama-cloud/glm-5.3
```

### OpenCode (`opencode`, `opencode-go`, and Anthropic Messages siblings)

```sh
poo login opencode
```

Stores a single OpenCode Console key (`OPENCODE_API_KEY`) shared across four built-in endpoints (your workspace plan determines which endpoints bill it):

- **Chat Completions**: `opencode` (`https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1`) and `opencode-go` (`https://opencode.ai/inference/go/openai/v1`)
- **Anthropic Messages**: `opencode-anthropic` (`https://opencode.ai/inference/anthropic/v1`) and `opencode-go-anthropic` (`https://opencode.ai/inference/go/anthropic/v1`), configured with `api: anthropic_messages`

```yaml
roles:
  chat: opencode-go/glm-5.3
  # Or use the Anthropic Messages sibling:
  # chat: opencode-go-anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5
```

All four endpoints probe the gateway's live model list and declare `session_header: x-opencode-session`, which causes `poo`'s transports to attach the session ID on every turn, fork, and compaction request. The Anthropic Messages transport handles content blocks, streamed tool call arguments, thinking blocks with preserved signatures, adaptive effort (`output_config.effort`), and token thinking budgets.

### TypeSafe (`typesafe`)

```sh
poo login typesafe
```

Stores a TypeSafe Console key (`TYPESAFE_API_KEY`) for `https://api.typesafe.ai/v1`. TypeSafe serves Jev decision models (`jev-latest`, `jev-preview`) that declare `ops: [systemone]` — they answer `decider` queries and cannot serve `chat` turns. See [Decision Model](/capabilities/decision-model).

```yaml
roles:
  chat: opencode-go/glm-5.3
  decider: typesafe/jev-latest
```

The built-in endpoint sets `instructions_per_question: true` (folding framing into each question because the API rejects request-level `instructions`) and `skip_probe: true` (its model list is not OpenAI-shaped). To add a newer Jev model before a binary release, declare it under `models` on the `typesafe` endpoint with `ops: [systemone]`.

## Custom Endpoints

Declare custom OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic Messages servers under `endpoints` and `models` in settings (or in a [Models File](/reference/models-file)):

```yaml
endpoints:
  local-vllm:
    endpoint: http://localhost:8000/v1
    api_key_env: LOCAL_VLLM_KEY
  anthropic-gateway:
    endpoint: https://gateway.example.com/anthropic/v1
    api_key_env: GATEWAY_API_KEY
    session_header: x-session-id
    skip_probe: true

models:
  local-qwen:
    endpoint: local-vllm
    model_id: Qwen/Qwen3-32B
    api: chat_completions
  gateway-claude:
    endpoint: anthropic-gateway
    model_id: claude-sonnet-4-5
    api: anthropic_messages

roles:
  chat: gateway-claude
```

### Endpoint Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `endpoint` | `string` | Base URL for the provider API (required). |
| `api_key_env` | `string` | Environment variable holding the API key (checked before credential files and `api_key`). |
| `api_key` | `string` | Literal API key fallback when `api_key_env` is unset. |
| `session_header` | `string` | HTTP header name carrying the session ID on turns, forks, and compactions. |
| `skip_probe` | `bool` | Skip `GET /models` discovery when the endpoint does not expose an OpenAI-compatible model list. |
| `instructions_per_question` | `bool` | Fold decider framing into each question instead of sending a request-level `instructions` field. |

### Wire APIs (`api`)

Each model (or endpoint in a models file) selects its wire transport with `api`:

- `chat_completions` (default when omitted) — OpenAI Chat Completions API.
- `anthropic_messages` — Anthropic Messages API (content blocks, streaming tools, thinking signatures, effort/budget controls).
- `responses` — OpenAI Responses API (used by the built-in `openai-codex` transport).

See [Wire API Mapping](/reference/wire-api-mapping) for exact request/response field mappings across transports.

## Verification Workflow

Run these two read-only checks before starting a session. Neither prints secrets nor trades tokens.

### Check Stored Credentials (`poo auth status`)

```sh
poo auth status [--settings /path/to/settings.yaml] [--json]
```

Reports the resolved file path, format (`poo`, `pi`, or Codex CLI), provider, OAuth client ID (if recorded), account ID, expiry timestamp, and state:

- `live` — Ready to use as-is (always `live` for API keys).
- `refresh needed` — OAuth access token is expired or within leeway; `poo` will refresh it on use or on `poo auth refresh`.
- `no readable expiry` — OAuth token has no readable `exp` claim.
- `expired (read-only: refresh with the tool that owns the file)` — Expired token in an `auth_readonly: true` file.

Pass `--json` for machine-readable output (`file`, `format`, `provider`, `client_id`, `account_id`, `expires`, `state`).

### Verify Role Resolution (`poo roles`)

```sh
poo roles [--settings /path/to/settings.yaml]
```

Builds the catalog the same way a session does and prints each [role](/configuration/models-and-catalog#roles-and-required-operations) (`chat`, `compaction`, `decider`) with its resolved `MODEL`, `PROVIDER`, and `CREDENTIAL` source (`env:<VAR>`, `static`, or `none`). Exits non-zero if any assigned role fails to resolve, listing candidate models that would satisfy it.
