<!-- Source: reference/cli.md -->

# CLI Reference

Every command, flag, and help text in `poo` comes from a single declaration in `cmd/poo/app.go`. Run `poo <command> --help` or `poo help <command>` for the exact usage of any command, or `poo --version` for the short build version.

## Front Door

A bare `poo` launches the front-door interface linked into the binary — `repl` by default, or whichever linked interface the resolved settings file names under `ui`. If no settings file exists yet, a bare `poo` on a terminal runs the interactive welcome flow; non-interactively, it exits `1`.

Three top-level shortcuts dispatch directly without naming a subcommand:

| Invocation | Equivalent | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `poo` | `poo repl` (or `ui` setting) | Launches the configured front-door UI with the discovered settings file. |
| `poo -p <prompt> [flags]` | `poo run [flags] -- <prompt>` | Runs a one-shot session. `--print` is an alias for `-p`. Accepts `run` and shared flags before or after the prompt; `--` ends flag parsing. |
| `poo -c [flags]` | `poo repl --continue [flags]` | Reopens the most recent session in the working directory. `--continue` is the long form. |
| `poo --resume <id> [flags]` | `poo repl --resume <id> [flags]` | Reopens the session identified by `<id>`. Mutually exclusive with `-c`/`--continue`. |

```bash
# One-shot prompt with flags after the prompt
poo -p "Summarize the git log" --max-turns 4 --ephemeral

# Reopen the latest session in this directory
poo -c

# Reopen a specific session by ID
poo --resume 0195c8a2-7b1e-7000-8000-000000000001
```

## Shared Flags

Every subcommand accepts these common flags. Precedence is profile, then settings file, then CLI flags (last writer wins), except repeated manifest path flags append to the settings' paths. See [Settings Discovery](/configuration/settings-discovery) for how `--settings` is resolved when omitted.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--settings` | string | discovered | Path to the settings file (JSON, TOML, or YAML). |
| `--system-prompt` | string | — | File holding the system prompt's base section. |
| `--append-system-prompt` | string | — | Text appended to the system prompt, or `@file` to read from a file. |
| `--permission-unmatched` | string | profile/settings | Action for side-effecting tool calls no rule covers: `allow`, `ask`, or `deny`. |
| `--session-dir` | string | settings | Directory where session files are stored. |
| `--user-prompt-file` | string | platform config `AGENTS.md` | File holding the user's own instructions. |
| `--ephemeral` | bool | `false` | Run without writing a session to disk. |
| `--profile` | string | settings / `code` | Profile to run under (for example `base`, `code`, `search`, or a custom profile). |
| `--feeds-path` | string (repeatable) | — | Additional feed manifest path. |
| `--mcp-path` | string (repeatable) | — | Additional MCP manifest path. |
| `--cli-registry-path` | string (repeatable) | — | Additional CLI registry manifest path. |

## Endpoint Flags

`run`, `repl`, `serve`, and `daemon` accept these endpoint flags to define or override the `chat` model on the command line. When any endpoint flag is supplied, `--endpoint`, `--model-id`, and a positive `--context-limit` are all required.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--endpoint` | string | — | OpenAI-compatible endpoint URL, e.g. `http://localhost:4000/v1`. |
| `--model-id` | string | — | Model identifier sent to the endpoint. |
| `--context-limit` | int | `0` | Model's context window in tokens (required and `> 0` when using endpoint flags). |
| `--api-key-env` | string | — | Name of the environment variable holding the API key. |
| `--tools-mode` | string | `native` | How tool calls are requested: `native`, `text`, or `auto`. |

## Subcommands

### `poo run`

Run a single one-shot session. The final answer is written to stdout and progress/diagnostics to stderr. Flags stop at the first non-flag argument, so everything from the first prompt word onward is prompt text. Use `poo -p` to place flags after the prompt.

Unless the settings file assigns a `chat` role, `--endpoint`, `--model-id`, and `--context-limit` are required. See [Limits & Exit Codes](/operations/limits-and-exit-codes) for exit codes and signal handling.

**Positional arguments:** `prompt...` (required, variadic)

**Flags:** Accepts [Shared Flags](#shared-flags), [Endpoint Flags](#endpoint-flags), and:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--permission-fallback` | string | settings | Decision when the permission asker chain is exhausted: `allow` or `deny`. |
| `--reasoning-effort` | string | settings | Reasoning level to send: `default` (no field), `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `xhigh`. |
| `--max-turns` | int | `0` (unlimited) | Turn limit for the run. |
| `--max-output` | int | model default | Override the model's output-token limit. |
| `--truncation-retries` | int | `1` | Consecutive output-limit truncations to retry more concisely before settling (`0` disables retries). |
| `--context-strategy` | string | `mine` | Compaction strategy: `summary`, `mine`, `pointer`, `native`, `handoff`, or `none`. |
| `--context-keep-recent` | int | strategy default | Verbatim tail retained by block compaction strategies (`summary`, `mine`, `pointer`), in tokens. |
| `--log` | string | — | Write session records to a specific JSONL file instead of the session store. |
| `--working-dir` | string | current directory | Working directory for tools (must exist). |
| `--executor` | string | `local` | Bash tool executor: `local` or `bwrap`. |
| `--project-prompt` | bool | `false` | Include the working directory's `AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md`) in the system prompt. |
| `--timeout` | duration | — | Wall-clock context deadline for the run, e.g. `5m`. |
| `--no-wait-jobs` | bool | `false` | Exit at the first settle instead of waiting for background jobs; running jobs stop on close. |

```bash
poo run --max-turns 12 --timeout 5m --project-prompt "Find and fix the failing unit test."

poo run --endpoint http://localhost:4000/v1 --model-id gemma4 \
  --context-limit 262144 --log session.jsonl \
  "List the Go packages in this repository."
```

---

### `poo repl`

Launch an interactive terminal session with vi keybindings and markdown rendering. Starts `poo serve` as a child process and forwards supplied shared, endpoint, and tool flags to it. Type `/help` inside the REPL for interactive commands. See [Interactive REPL](/getting-started/repl).

**Flags:** Accepts [Shared Flags](#shared-flags), [Endpoint Flags](#endpoint-flags), and:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--working-dir` | string | current directory | Working directory for tools. |
| `--executor` | string | `local` | Bash tool executor: `local` or `bwrap`. |
| `-c`, `--continue` | bool | `false` | Continue the most recent session in the working directory. |
| `--resume` | string | — | Resume the session named by this ID. |

```bash
poo repl --working-dir ./my-repo --executor bwrap
poo repl --resume 0195c8a2-7b1e-7000-8000-000000000001
```

---

### `poo serve`

Serve the JSON-RPC 2.0 wire protocol over stdin and stdout (one JSON object per line). See [Wire Protocol](/extending/wire-protocol).

**Flags:** Accepts [Shared Flags](#shared-flags), [Endpoint Flags](#endpoint-flags), and:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--working-dir` | string | current directory | Working directory for tools. |
| `--executor` | string | `local` | Bash tool executor: `local` or `bwrap`. |

```bash
poo serve --profile code --working-dir /srv/project
```

---

### `poo daemon`

Host a long-lived, feed-driven session without reading stdin. Defaults the session mode to `durable` when neither `--ephemeral` nor `session.mode` is set, starts all non-optional feeds, and writes lifecycle events one fact per line to stderr. See [Feeds & Daemon](/capabilities/feeds-and-daemon) and [Daemon Exit Codes](/operations/limits-and-exit-codes#poo-daemon-exit-codes).

**Flags:** Accepts [Shared Flags](#shared-flags), [Endpoint Flags](#endpoint-flags), and:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--session` | string | generated | Session ID to load, or create if it does not exist. When omitted, a new ID is generated and printed to stderr. |
| `--auto-resume` | bool | `true` | Resume a pending unsettled run automatically on load. |
| `--working-dir` | string | current directory | Working directory for tools. |

```bash
poo daemon --session ops-watcher --working-dir /srv/app
poo daemon --session ops-watcher --auto-resume=false
```

---

### `poo models`

List the effective model catalog — combining settings, `models_file`, curated built-ins, and live endpoint probes — or explain where each field of a single model came from. See [Models & Catalog](/configuration/models-and-catalog).

**Flags:** Accepts [Shared Flags](#shared-flags) and:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Print the model list as JSON. |
| `--explain` | string | — | Print each field of the named model and the catalog layer that set it. |

```bash
poo models
poo models --json
poo models --explain codex/gpt-5.4
```

---

### `poo roles`

Resolve every configured role (`chat`, `decider`, `compaction`, and any additional assigned roles) against the catalog and print the model, provider, and credential source (`env:<VAR>`, `static`, or `none`). Prints no secrets, trades no credentials, and exits `1` if any assigned role fails to resolve.

**Flags:** Accepts [Shared Flags](#shared-flags) only.

```bash
poo roles
poo roles --settings ./codex.settings.yaml
```

---

### `poo prompt`

Print the exact rendered system prompt a session would send to the model. Does not require a configured chat model. See [Profiles & Prompts](/configuration/profiles-and-prompts).

**Flags:** Accepts [Shared Flags](#shared-flags) and:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--project-prompt` | bool | `false` | Include the working directory's `AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md`) in the prompt. |
| `--pretty` | bool | `false` | Format each section under a `--- <name> ---` header and summarize the skill catalog. |

```bash
poo prompt --pretty --project-prompt
poo prompt --profile search
```

---

### `poo login`

Sign in to a provider and store the credential in `auth_file` (or poo's default `auth.json`). Keys are read from an interactive terminal prompt or stdin — never via a flag. Existing credentials are not overwritten unless confirmed interactively or forced with `--force`. See [Providers & Auth](/configuration/providers-and-auth).

**Positional arguments:** `[provider]` (optional). Supported providers:

- `codex` — OpenAI Codex (browser OAuth sign-in with loopback callback or URL paste fallback)
- `ollama-cloud` — Ollama Cloud (API key)
- `opencode` — OpenCode (API key)
- `typesafe` — TypeSafe (API key)

A bare `poo login` presents the provider list interactively.

**Flags:** Accepts [Shared Flags](#shared-flags) and:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--force` | bool | `false` | Replace an existing credential without asking. |
| `--no-browser` | bool | `false` | Print the sign-in URL instead of opening a browser. |
| `--wait` | int | `300` | Seconds to wait for a browser sign-in callback. |

```bash
poo login codex
poo login codex --no-browser --wait 600
printf '%s' "$OPENCODE_API_KEY" | poo login opencode --force
```

---

### `poo auth status`

Report the resolved credential file, file format, provider, OAuth client, account ID, expiry, and state (`live`, `refresh needed`, `no readable expiry`, or expired under a read-only file). Prints no secrets and does not refresh tokens.

**Flags:** Accepts [Shared Flags](#shared-flags) and:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Print the status report as JSON. |

```bash
poo auth status
poo auth status --json
```

---

### `poo auth refresh`

Refresh the OpenAI Codex credential in the resolved credential file when the access token is within the leeway window of expiring. Exits `0` silently on success (including when no refresh is due) and non-zero on failure.

**Flags:** Accepts [Shared Flags](#shared-flags) and:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--leeway` | duration | `5m` | Refresh when this much time or less remains before expiry (must be positive). |
| `--force` | bool | `false` | Refresh immediately even if the access token is still fresh. |

```bash
poo auth refresh
poo auth refresh --leeway 15m
poo auth refresh --force
```

---

### `poo auth import pi`

Copy the OpenAI Codex credential from pi's `auth.json` into poo's credential file. Because OAuth refresh rotates the refresh token, only one tool can keep the imported credential alive after the first refresh. Does not modify pi's file.

**Flags:** Accepts [Shared Flags](#shared-flags) and:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--from` | string | `pi_auth_file`, then `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` | Source `auth.json` file to copy from. |
| `--force` | bool | `false` | Replace an existing credential in poo's file without asking. |

```bash
poo auth import pi
poo auth import pi --from ~/.pi/agent/auth.json --force
```

---

### `poo sessions list`

List sessions in the session store with columns `ID`, `CREATED`, `PROFILE`, `RUNS`, `REASON`, `SIZE`, and `LOCKED`. See [Sessions & Durability](/operations/sessions-and-durability).

**Flags:** Accepts [Shared Flags](#shared-flags) and:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Print the session summaries as JSON. |

```bash
poo sessions list
poo sessions list --json --session-dir /var/lib/poo/sessions
```

---

### `poo sessions prune`

Delete sessions matched by the retention policy (`session.retention` in settings, overridden by flags). Locked sessions are skipped and reported on stderr. Exits `2` if neither settings nor flags specify a retention policy.

**Flags:** Accepts [Shared Flags](#shared-flags) and:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--older-than` | int | settings (`max_age_days`) | Delete sessions whose last activity is older than this many days. |
| `--keep` | int | settings (`max_sessions`) | Keep this many most recently active sessions. |
| `--dry-run` | bool | `false` | Print sessions that would be deleted without deleting anything. |

```bash
poo sessions prune --older-than 30 --dry-run
poo sessions prune --keep 20
```

---

### `poo version`

Print the binary's version, VCS revision, commit timestamp, dirty/modified status, and Go toolchain version embedded by the Go build.

**Flags:** Accepts [Shared Flags](#shared-flags) and:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Print build information as JSON (`version`, `revision`, `time`, `modified`, `go_version`). |

```bash
poo version
poo version --json
poo --version
```

---

<!-- Source: reference/settings.md -->

# Settings Reference

Every key in a poo settings file is optional except `version`. Unknown keys are rejected at load time. See [Settings Discovery](/configuration/settings-discovery) for file lookup order, supported formats, and relative path resolution rules.

## Top-Level Metadata & Interface

### `version`

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | `int` | Required (`1`) | Settings format version. Must be `1`. |

### `ui`

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ui` | `string` | Binary's default front door (`repl`) | Interface launched by a bare `poo` invocation. Must be linked into the binary. |

## Profiles

See [Profiles & Prompts](/configuration/profiles-and-prompts) for profile inheritance and layering details.

### `profile` & `repl_profile`

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `profile` | `string` | Binary's default profile | Profile name used when building a session (`run`, `serve`, etc.). |
| `repl_profile` | `string` | Falls back to `profile` / binary default | Profile used by the interactive REPL for new conversations when no flag overrides it. Reopened sessions keep the profile recorded in their log. |

### `profiles_files`

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `profiles_files` | `string[]` | Empty | External YAML or JSON files defining reusable profiles under a top-level `profiles` key. Loaded as layers below inline `profiles` (inline wins, then earlier files). Relative paths resolve against the settings file's directory; `prompt_file` and `prompt_append_file` inside a profiles file resolve against that profiles file's directory. |

### `profiles`

Map of `<name>` to profile definition object. Each entry defines a named variant of a linked profile or another defined profile.

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `profiles.<name>.base` | `string` | Required | Name of the linked or defined profile this profile inherits from. |
| `profiles.<name>.mcp_defaults` | `bool` | Inherits `mcp.defaults` | Overrides whether poo's default `mcp` directory loads for sessions under this profile. |
| `profiles.<name>.mcp_servers` | `string[]` | Inherits base | MCP server names to start. Appends to the base profile's list (deduplicated, preserving first appearance). Missing servers warn and are skipped. |
| `profiles.<name>.feeds` | `string[]` | Inherits base | Feed manifest names this profile requires. Appends to the base profile's list (deduplicated). Unloaded feeds warn and are skipped. |
| `profiles.<name>.feeds_defaults` | `bool` | Inherits `feeds.defaults` | Overrides whether poo's default `feeds` directory loads for sessions under this profile. |
| `profiles.<name>.cli_registry_defaults` | `bool` | Inherits `cli_registry.defaults` | Overrides whether poo's default `cli-registry` directory loads for sessions under this profile. |
| `profiles.<name>.prompt_file` | `string` | Empty | File whose text replaces the profile's prompt section. Relative paths resolve against the declaring file's directory. |
| `profiles.<name>.prompt_append_file` | `string` | Empty | File whose text appends to the profile's prompt section. Mutually exclusive with `prompt_append`. Relative paths resolve against the declaring file's directory. |
| `profiles.<name>.prompt_append` | `string` | Empty | Inline text appended to the profile's prompt section. Mutually exclusive with `prompt_append_file`. |
| `profiles.<name>.model_family` | `bool` | `false` | When `true`, includes model-family guidance keyed by the active model's `prompt_variant`. |
| `profiles.<name>.tools.disabled` | `string[]` | Empty | Tool names disabled for sessions running under this profile. |

```yaml
profile: reviewer
repl_profile: code
profiles_files:
  - ./team-profiles.yaml

profiles:
  reviewer:
    base: code
    prompt_append: "Focus on correctness and edge cases. Do not modify files."
    model_family: true
    tools:
      disabled: [edit, write, bash]
```

## Endpoints, Models, Roles & Auth

See [Models & Catalog](/configuration/models-and-catalog), [Models File Reference](/reference/models-file), and [Providers & Auth](/configuration/providers-and-auth).

### `endpoints`

Map of `<name>` to endpoint configuration object. Credentials resolve from `api_key_env` first, falling back to literal `api_key`.

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `endpoints.<name>.endpoint` | `string` | Required | Base URL for the endpoint (legacy alias: `base_url`). |
| `endpoints.<name>.api_key_env` | `string` | Empty | Environment variable name holding the API key. Automatically scrubbed from child tool environments. |
| `endpoints.<name>.api_key` | `string` | Empty | Literal API key stored in settings (fallback when `api_key_env` is unset or empty). |
| `endpoints.<name>.session_header` | `string` | Empty | HTTP header name that carries the session ID for gateway routing. |
| `endpoints.<name>.skip_probe` | `bool` | `false` | Skip probing the endpoint for its served model list. |
| `endpoints.<name>.instructions_per_question` | `bool` | `false` | Fold decision framing into each question instead of sending a request-level `instructions` field. |

### `models`

Map of `<name>` to model configuration object. Omitted fields inherit from the curated catalog, `models_file`, or endpoint discovery.

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `models.<name>.endpoint` | `string` | Required | Name of the endpoint serving this model. |
| `models.<name>.model_id` | `string` | Required | Model identifier sent to the endpoint. |
| `models.<name>.api` | `string` | Chat completions | Wire API dialect used to talk to the model (e.g., `responses`). See [Wire API Mapping](/reference/wire-api-mapping). |
| `models.<name>.tools_mode` | `string` | Model default | How tool calls are requested: `native`, `text`, `auto`, or `none`. |
| `models.<name>.ops` | `string[]` | Model default | Operations the model serves (e.g., `compact` for native compaction). |
| `models.<name>.inputs` | `string[]` | Model default | Input modalities the model accepts (e.g., `text`, `image`). |
| `models.<name>.context_limit` | `int` | Model default | Total context window size in tokens (prompt plus output). |
| `models.<name>.input_limit` | `int` | Model default | Maximum prompt tokens accepted when smaller than `context_limit`. |
| `models.<name>.max_output` | `int` | Model default | Maximum tokens the model writes in one response. |
| `models.<name>.reasoning` | `object` | Model default | How reasoning is controlled on the wire. Contains `mode` (`none`, `toggle`, `effort`, `budget`) and `param` (wire parameter path, e.g., `reasoning_effort` or `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`). |
| `models.<name>.reasoning_levels` | `string[]` | Model default | Accepted reasoning levels from lowest to highest (e.g., `[off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh]`). Sent verbatim as spelled. |
| `models.<name>.quirks` | `string[]` | Empty | Named transport adaptations applied in order (e.g., `audio_url`). Unknown names warn and are skipped. |
| `models.<name>.prompt_variant` | `string` | Empty | Variant key used to select model-family prompt sections. |

### `models_file`

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `models_file` | `string` | Auto-discovers sibling `models.yaml` or `models.json` | Path to a models file loaded as a catalog layer below inline `endpoints` and `models` (legacy alias: `pi_models_file`). Relative paths resolve against the settings file's directory. |

### `roles`

Map of role name to model name (either a key in `models` or `<endpoint>/<id>` from `models_file` / built-in providers).

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `roles.chat` | `string` | None | Primary chat model for the session. |
| `roles.decider` | `string` | None | Decision model used by the `decide` permission asker and CLI registry filtering. See [Decision Model](/capabilities/decision-model). |
| `roles.compaction` | `string` | Falls back to `roles.chat` | Model used for compaction requests (`summary`, `mine`, `pointer`, `handoff`). |

### `auth_file`, `pi_auth_file` & `auth_readonly`

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auth_file` | `string` | Sibling `auth.yaml`/`auth.json` beside `models_file`, else platform config dir | Path to poo's credential file (or a shared read-only file such as `~/.codex/auth.json`). Mutually exclusive with `pi_auth_file`. Relative paths resolve against the settings file's directory. |
| `pi_auth_file` | `string` | None | Path to pi's `auth.json`, read and written in pi's format. Must exist. Mutually exclusive with `auth_file`. Relative paths resolve against the settings file's directory. |
| `auth_readonly` | `bool` | `false` | When `true`, poo never refreshes, signs in, imports, or writes the credential file. Use when another tool owns token refresh. |

```yaml
version: 1
models_file: ./models.yaml
auth_file: ~/.codex/auth.json
auth_readonly: true

endpoints:
  local:
    endpoint: http://localhost:4000/v1
    api_key_env: LOCAL_API_KEY

models:
  qwen3:
    endpoint: local
    model_id: qwen3-coder
    context_limit: 131072
    max_output: 8192
    tools_mode: auto

roles:
  chat: qwen3
  decider: local/gemma-decider
```

## Reasoning & Sampling

See [Reasoning & Sampling](/configuration/reasoning-and-sampling).

### `reasoning`

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reasoning.chat` | `string` | `default` | Reasoning level for the chat model: `default`, `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, or a positive integer token budget (e.g., `"8192"`). `default` omits the reasoning field; `off` asks the model not to think. |

### `sampling`

Map of `<model>` name to per-model sampling overrides. Omitted fields are not sent so the endpoint's default applies.

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sampling.<model>.temperature` | `float` | Unset | Sampling temperature. |
| `sampling.<model>.top_p` | `float` | Unset | Nucleus sampling threshold. |
| `sampling.<model>.top_k` | `float` | Unset | Number of candidate tokens considered by the sampler. |
| `sampling.<model>.min_p` | `float` | Unset | Minimum token probability threshold. |

```yaml
reasoning:
  chat: medium

sampling:
  qwen3:
    temperature: 0.6
    top_p: 0.95
```

## Decider

See [Decision Model](/capabilities/decision-model).

### `decider`

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `decider.timeout_ms` | `int` | Decider default | Per-call latency budget for the decider model, in milliseconds. Minimum `1`. |

## Context & Compaction

See [Context Compaction](/capabilities/compaction).

### `context`

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `context.strategy` | `string` | `mine` | Compaction strategy: `summary`, `mine`, `pointer`, `handoff`, `native`, or `none`. `native` requires a model declaring the `compact` op and a native-compacting transport. |
| `context.notice_ratio` | `float` | Removed (ignored) | Removed setting. Accepted for backward compatibility and emits a warning. |
| `context.hard_ratio` | `float` | Removed (ignored) | Removed setting. Accepted for backward compatibility and emits a warning. |
| `context.handoff.ratio` | `float` | Strategy default | Fraction of the prompt limit (`0`–`1`) that triggers handoff compaction. |
| `context.handoff.max_tokens` | `int` | Strategy default | Token limit for the handoff request (`≥ 0`). |
| `context.summary.ratio` | `float` | Strategy default | Fraction of the prompt limit (`0`–`1`) that triggers summary compaction. |
| `context.summary.keep_recent_tokens` | `int` | Strategy default | Recent history tokens kept verbatim (`≥ 0`). |
| `context.summary.max_tokens` | `int` | Strategy default | Token limit for the summary request (`≥ 0`). |
| `context.mine.ratio` | `float` | Strategy default | Fraction of the prompt limit (`0`–`1`) that triggers mine compaction. |
| `context.mine.keep_recent_tokens` | `int` | Strategy default | Recent history tokens kept verbatim (`≥ 0`). |
| `context.mine.max_tokens` | `int` | Strategy default | Token limit for the mining request (`≥ 0`). |
| `context.mine.pointer_max_tokens` | `int` | Strategy default | Token limit for the pointer pass (`≥ 0`). |
| `context.pointer.ratio` | `float` | Strategy default | Fraction of the prompt limit (`0`–`1`) that triggers pointer compaction. |
| `context.pointer.keep_recent_tokens` | `int` | Strategy default | Recent history tokens kept verbatim (`≥ 0`). |
| `context.pointer.max_tokens` | `int` | Strategy default | Token limit for the compose request (`≥ 0`). |
| `context.pointer.pointer_max_tokens` | `int` | Strategy default | Token limit for the pointer pass (`≥ 0`). |
| `context.pointer.snippet_budget` | `int` | Strategy default | Maximum bytes of snippet text collected by queries (`≥ 0`). |
| `context.pointer.escalate_after` | `int` | Strategy default | Number of pointer compactions before escalating to full-span fallback (`≥ 0`). |

```yaml
context:
  strategy: mine
  mine:
    ratio: 0.75
    keep_recent_tokens: 8192
```

## Tools & Sandboxing

See [Built-in Tools & Jobs](/capabilities/tools-and-jobs), [Codemode](/capabilities/codemode), and [Sandboxing (bwrap)](/operations/sandbox).

### `tools`

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tools.read.restrict_to_working_dir` | `bool` | `false` | Confine `read` to the session's working directory. |
| `tools.read.ask_outside_working_dir` | `bool` | `false` | Route `read` targets outside the working directory through the permission asker. |
| `tools.grep.restrict_to_working_dir` | `bool` | `false` | Confine `grep` to the session's working directory. |
| `tools.grep.ask_outside_working_dir` | `bool` | `false` | Route `grep` targets outside the working directory through the permission asker. |
| `tools.edit.restrict_to_working_dir` | `bool` | `false` | Confine `edit` to the session's working directory. |
| `tools.edit.ask_outside_working_dir` | `bool` | `false` | Route `edit` targets outside the working directory through the permission asker. |
| `tools.write.restrict_to_working_dir` | `bool` | `false` | Confine `write` to the session's working directory. |
| `tools.write.ask_outside_working_dir` | `bool` | `false` | Route `write` targets outside the working directory through the permission asker. |
| `tools.bash.timeout_s` | `int` | `120` | Per-command wall-clock timeout, in seconds. |
| `tools.bash.executor` | `string` | `local` | Command executor linked into the binary (e.g., `local`, `bwrap`). |
| `tools.codemode.engine` | `string` | `quickjs` | Script runtime for `codemode`: `quickjs` or `starlark`. |
| `tools.codemode.timeout_s` | `int` | Engine default | Wall-clock timeout for one script run, in seconds. |
| `tools.codemode.script_max_bytes` | `int` | Engine default | Maximum accepted script size, in bytes. |
| `tools.codemode.output_cap_chars` | `int` | Engine default | Maximum printed output characters retained per run. |
| `tools.codemode.exec_steps` | `int` | Engine default | Starlark execution step budget. Rejected if non-zero when `engine` is `quickjs`. |
| `tools.fetch.timeout_s` | `int` | `30` | Timeout per HTTP fetch, in seconds. |
| `tools.fetch.max_bytes` | `int` | Tool default | Maximum response body size read, in bytes. |
| `tools.fetch.user_agent` | `string` | Tool default | Custom `User-Agent` header sent by `fetch`. |
| `tools.fetch.allow_private_hosts` | `bool` | `false` | Allow loopback and private IP ranges in `fetch` (link-local and reserved ranges remain blocked). |
| `tools.bwrap.network` | `bool` | `true` | Share host network inside the `bwrap` sandbox. Set `false` to isolate network access. |
| `tools.bwrap.ro_binds` | `string[]` | `/usr`, `/bin`, `/lib`, `/lib64`, `/etc` | Host paths mounted read-only inside the `bwrap` sandbox. |
| `tools.bwrap.rw_binds` | `string[]` | Working dir only | Additional host paths mounted read-write inside the `bwrap` sandbox. |
| `tools.env.scrub` | `string[]` | Endpoint credential env vars | Environment variable names removed from child processes and session environment. |
| `tools.env.passthrough` | `string[]` | Unset (all non-scrubbed vars) | Allowlist of environment variable names kept for child processes; all others are dropped. |
| `tools.protected_paths` | `string[]` | Empty | Glob patterns of paths tools must not read or modify (masked inside `bwrap`). |
| `tools.disabled` | `string[]` | Empty | Tool names disabled regardless of profile. Naming an unlinked or core-required tool is an error. |

```yaml
tools:
  edit:
    restrict_to_working_dir: true
  write:
    restrict_to_working_dir: true
  bash:
    executor: bwrap
    timeout_s: 60
  bwrap:
    network: false
  protected_paths:
    - "**/.env"
    - "~/.ssh/**"
  disabled: [fetch]
```

## Permissions

See [Permissions & Safety](/operations/permissions-and-safety).

### `permission`

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `permission.unmatched` | `string` | Profile default | Action for a side-effecting call that matches no rule: `allow`, `ask`, or `deny`. |
| `permission.fallback` | `string` | `deny` | Decision when the asker chain is exhausted or times out: `allow` or `deny`. |
| `permission.askers` | `string[]` | Binary's default chain | Ordered list of askers (`decide`, `wire`). An explicit empty list `[]` skips all askers and goes straight to `fallback`. `decide` requires `roles.decider`. |
| `permission.chain_timeout_s` | `int` | `120` | Overall timeout for the asker chain, in seconds. Minimum `1`. |
| `permission.doom_loop.threshold` | `int` | Policy default | Exact repeat count that triggers the doom-loop action. Minimum `1`. |
| `permission.doom_loop.near_threshold` | `int` | Policy default | Near-repeat count that triggers the doom-loop action. Minimum `1`. |
| `permission.doom_loop.action` | `string` | Policy default | Action taken on a doom loop: `allow`, `ask`, or `deny`. |
| `permission.decide.allow` | `float` | `0.85` | Probability threshold (`0`–`1`) at which the decider allows a call. Requires `roles.decider`. |
| `permission.decide.deny` | `float` | `0.99` | Probability threshold (`0`–`1`) at which the decider denies a call. Requires `roles.decider`. |
| `permission.decide.timeout_ms` | `int` | `1500` | Per-call timeout for the `decide` asker, in milliseconds. Minimum `1`. Requires `roles.decider`. |
| `permission.rules` | `object[]` | Empty | Ordered permission rules; first match wins. See table below. |

### `permission.rules[]`

Each rule must specify **either** `tool` **or** `class` (never both). `command_prefix` and `command_contains` require `tool` and are mutually exclusive.

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tool` | `string` | Empty | Tool name to match (must be linked into the binary). |
| `class` | `string` | Empty | Tool class to match: `read_only` or `side_effecting`. |
| `command_prefix` | `string` | Empty | Prefix matched against the tool's primary argument (e.g., bash command or fetch URL). A schemeless URL prefix matches both `http` and `https`. |
| `command_contains` | `string[]` | Empty | Non-empty substrings matched anywhere in the tool's primary argument (any single match triggers). |
| `action` | `string` | Required | Action on match: `allow`, `ask`, or `deny`. |

```yaml
permission:
  unmatched: ask
  fallback: deny
  askers: [decide, wire]
  chain_timeout_s: 60
  rules:
    - class: read_only
      action: allow
    - tool: bash
      command_prefix: "git status"
      action: allow
    - tool: bash
      command_contains: ["rm -rf", "sudo "]
      action: deny
```

## System Prompt

See [Profiles & Prompts](/configuration/profiles-and-prompts).

### `system_prompt`

`base_file` and `replace` are mutually exclusive.

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_prompt.base_file` | `string` | Empty | File holding the prompt's base section. Relative paths resolve against the settings file's directory; `~/` resolves under `$HOME`. |
| `system_prompt.replace` | `string` | Empty | Inline text replacing the entire prompt (except the CLI catalog section when active). |
| `system_prompt.append` | `string` | Empty | Text appended to the base prompt section. |
| `system_prompt.sections` | `map[string]string` | Empty | Named prompt sections to set or override. |
| `system_prompt.remove` | `string[]` | Empty | Named prompt sections to remove. |

## Limits & Background Jobs

See [Limits & Exit Codes](/operations/limits-and-exit-codes) and [Built-in Tools & Jobs](/capabilities/tools-and-jobs).

### `limits`

A value of `0` disables the limit (except `truncation_retries`, where `0` disables retries and omission uses the default of `1`).

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limits.max_tokens_per_run` | `int` | `0` (off) | Maximum tokens consumed in a single run (`≥ 0`). |
| `limits.max_duration_s` | `int` | `0` (off) | Wall-clock time limit for a single run, in seconds (`≥ 0`). |
| `limits.max_turns` | `int` | `0` (off) | Maximum model turns in a single run (`≥ 0`). |
| `limits.max_continuations` | `int` | `0` (off) | Maximum continuations allowed in a run (`≥ 0`). |
| `limits.truncation_retries` | `int` | `1` | Consecutive truncated turns retried before settling `output_truncated`. Set `0` to disable (`≥ 0`). |

### `jobs`

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `jobs.max_running` | `int` | Runtime default | Maximum concurrent background jobs (`≥ 0`). |
| `jobs.timeout_s` | `int` | Runtime default | Per-job wall-clock timeout, in seconds (`≥ 0`). |
| `jobs.on_idle` | `string` | Runtime default | Handling for a job result arriving while the session is idle: `wake` or `hold`. |
| `jobs.max_unattended_wakes` | `int` | `0` (no limit) | Maximum consecutive woken runs without client input (`≥ 0`). |

## Structured Output

### `finish`

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `finish.schema_file` | `string` | Empty | Path to a valid JSON Schema file used to validate typed final results. Relative paths resolve against the settings file's directory; `~/` resolves under `$HOME`. |

## Manifests & Skills

See [CLI Registry & Script Tools](/capabilities/cli-registry), [Feeds & Daemon](/capabilities/feeds-and-daemon), [MCP Servers](/capabilities/mcp-servers), [Skills](/capabilities/skills), and [Manifests Reference](/reference/manifests).

### `cli_registry`

Legacy alias: `cliregistry`.

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cli_registry.paths` | `string[]` | Empty | Registry directories. Relative paths resolve against the working directory; `~/` resolves under `$HOME`. |
| `cli_registry.defaults` | `bool` | `true` | Load manifests from poo's default `cli-registry` directory under the user config directory. Set `false` to isolate. |

### `feeds`

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `feeds.paths` | `string[]` | Empty | Feed manifest directories. Relative paths resolve against the working directory; `~/` resolves under `$HOME`. |
| `feeds.defaults` | `bool` | `true` | Load manifests from poo's default `feeds` directory under the user config directory. Set `false` to isolate. |

### `mcp`

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mcp.paths` | `string[]` | Empty | `mcp.json` manifest files or directories. Relative paths resolve against the working directory; `~/` resolves under `$HOME`. |
| `mcp.defaults` | `bool` | `true` | Load manifests from poo's default `mcp` directory under the user config directory. Set `false` to isolate. |

### `skills`

`default` and `user_path` are mutually exclusive. Missing skill directories are dropped with a warning (silently for `default`).

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skills.default` | `bool` | `false` | When `true`, offer skills from `~/.agents/skills`. Mutually exclusive with `user_path`. |
| `skills.user_path` | `string` | Empty | Custom user skills directory (`~/` expanded). Mutually exclusive with `default`. |
| `skills.paths` | `string[]` | Empty | Additional skill directories. Relative paths resolve against the working directory; `~/` resolves under `$HOME`. |

## Session Persistence & Prompts

See [Sessions & Durability](/operations/sessions-and-durability).

### `session`

| Key | Type | Default / Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `session.mode` | `string` | `logged` | Session persistence mode: `logged`, `ephemeral`, or `durable`. |
| `session.dir` | `string` | `~/.local/state/poo/sessions` | Directory where session logs and state live (`~/` expanded). |
| `session.project_prompt` | `bool` | `false` | Include the working directory's `AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md` if absent) in the prompt. Reads only the working directory; never walks up. |
| `session.user_prompt` | `bool` | `false` | Load user instructions from the binary's default config path. |
| `session.user_prompt_file` | `string` | Empty | Path to a custom user instructions file (`~/` expanded). Setting this enables user instructions without setting `user_prompt: true`. |
| `session.retention.max_age_days` | `int` | Unset (opt-in) | Delete sessions whose last activity is older than this many days on prune (`≥ 0`). |
| `session.retention.max_sessions` | `int` | Unset (opt-in) | Keep at most this many sessions on prune (`≥ 0`). |
| `session.durable.max_resumptions` | `int` | `3` | Maximum crash resumptions before the durable planner gives up. Minimum `1`. |
| `session.durable.lease_ttl_s` | `int` | `30` | Session lease duration before expiry, in seconds. Minimum `1`. |
| `session.durable.auto_resume` | `bool` | `false` | Automatically resume an unsettled run when a durable session loads. |
| `session.durable.store` | `string` | `file` | Durable storage backend: `file` or `sqlite`. |

```yaml
session:
  mode: durable
  dir: ~/.local/state/poo/sessions
  project_prompt: true
  retention:
    max_age_days: 30
    max_sessions: 200
  durable:
    store: sqlite
    max_resumptions: 3
    lease_ttl_s: 30
    auto_resume: false
```

<!-- Source: reference/models-file.md -->

# Models File Reference

A models file declares endpoints and the models each endpoint serves. It populates the catalog's `models_file` layer, below `settings.yaml` and above `curated` and `discovery` (see [Models & Catalog](/configuration/models-and-catalog)).

## Discovery and Format

poo locates a models file in this order:

1. The path set by `models_file` in `settings.yaml`. Relative paths resolve against the **settings file's directory**; `~/` resolves under the home directory.
2. Otherwise, if `settings.yaml` was loaded from disk, poo looks for `models.yaml` or `models.json` in the same directory.
   - If **both** `models.yaml` and `models.json` exist beside `settings.yaml`, loading fails with an error so neither file is silently ignored.
   - If a models file exists (or is explicitly named) and fails to read or validate, loading fails.

Both YAML and JSON are accepted through the same parser (leading UTF-8 BOMs are stripped). A file with a top-level `providers` key is imported as a [pi `models.json`](#pi-models-json-import); otherwise it is parsed as poo's native `models.yaml` format.

## Native `models.yaml` Schema

poo decodes `models.yaml` **strictly**: any unknown key is an error. The file must declare at least one endpoint, and each endpoint must declare at least one model.

Every model declared under endpoint `<ep>` and key `<id>` is registered in the catalog under the name **`<ep>/<id>`**.

```yaml
endpoints:
  home:
    endpoint: http://localhost:4000/v1
    api: chat_completions
    api_key_env: HOME_API_KEY
    session_header: x-session-id
    skip_probe: false
    instructions_per_question: false
    models:
      qwen3:
        model_id: qwen3-32b
        ops: [chat, systemone]
        inputs: [text, image]
        context_limit: 131072
        input_limit: 65536
        max_output: 16384
        tools_mode: auto
        reasoning:
          mode: toggle
          param: chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking
        reasoning_levels: [off, high]
        prompt_variant: qwen
        quirks: [think_tags]
        sampling:
          temperature: 0.7
          top_p: 0.9
          top_k: 40
          min_p: 0.05
```

### Top-Level Keys

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `endpoints` | `map<string, Endpoint>` | Yes | Map of endpoint names to endpoint definitions. Must be non-empty. |

### Endpoint Keys (`endpoints.<name>`)

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `endpoint` | `string` | Yes | Base URL of the endpoint (e.g. `http://localhost:4000/v1`). |
| `api` | `string` | No | Wire API spoken by the endpoint: `chat_completions` (default when omitted), `responses`, or `anthropic_messages`. Inherited by models under this endpoint. |
| `api_key_env` | `string` | No | Environment variable holding the API key. Also matched against stored key providers in the auth file (see [Providers & Auth](/configuration/providers-and-auth)). |
| `api_key` | `string` | **Refused** | **Always rejected.** See [Literal `api_key` Refusal](#literal-api-key-refusal). |
| `session_header` | `string` | No | HTTP header name that carries the session ID on requests (for gateways that route a conversation's requests together). |
| `skip_probe` | `bool` | No | When `true`, skips discovery probing for this endpoint. Use for endpoints without a discoverable model list. |
| `instructions_per_question` | `bool` | No | When `true`, folds decider instructions into each question instead of sending a request-level `instructions` field. |
| `models` | `map<string, Model>` | Yes | Map of model keys to model definitions. Must be non-empty. |

### Model Keys (`endpoints.<name>.models.<id>`)

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `model_id` | `string` | No | Wire model identifier sent to the endpoint. Defaults to the map key `<id>`. |
| `ops` | `string[]` | No | Supported operations: `chat`, `systemone`, `decisions`, `compact`. Defaults to `[chat]` if no layer sets it. |
| `inputs` | `string[]` | No | Supported input modalities: `text`, `image`, `audio`. Unknown modality names fail load. |
| `context_limit` | `int` | No | Total context window in tokens. |
| `input_limit` | `int` | No | Maximum prompt tokens accepted by the endpoint when smaller than `context_limit`. |
| `max_output` | `int` | No | Maximum output tokens per response. |
| `reasoning` | `object` | No | Reasoning control object with `mode` (`none`, `toggle`, `effort`, `budget`) and `param` (dot-path string). See [Reasoning & Sampling](/configuration/reasoning-and-sampling). |
| `reasoning_levels` | `string[]` | No | Accepted reasoning levels, lowest first (e.g. `[off, low, medium, high, xhigh]`). |
| `tools_mode` | `string` | No | Tool-calling mode: `native`, `text`, `auto`, or `none`. |
| `prompt_variant` | `string` | No | Prompt section variant key (used by model-family prompt guidance). |
| `quirks` | `string[]` | No | Ordered list of transport quirks (e.g. `think_tags`, `audio_url`). See [Transport Quirks](/configuration/reasoning-and-sampling#transport-quirks). |
| `sampling` | `object` | No | Model sampling defaults: `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, `min_p` (floats). |

### Literal `api_key` Refusal

A models file is designed to be shared or checked into version control. Writing a literal `api_key` on any endpoint in `models.yaml` fails load with an error. Instead:

- Set `api_key_env: MY_API_KEY` on the endpoint, or
- Store the credential in poo's auth file (`poo login`), or
- If you must write a literal key, put it on the endpoint in `settings.yaml` (which overrides the models file's endpoint).

## pi `models.json` Import

When a models file has a top-level `providers` key (or is a `models.json` written by `pi`), poo translates it into the `models_file` catalog layer under `<provider>/<model.id>`.

- **Forward compatibility**: pi fields that poo does not map are ignored rather than rejected.
- **Required fields**: at least one provider; each provider must have `baseUrl` and a non-empty `models` array; each model must have `id`.

### Field Mapping

| pi field | poo mapping / rule |
| :--- | :--- |
| `providers.<name>.baseUrl` | `endpoint` |
| `providers.<name>.api` | `""` or `openai-completions` → default (`chat_completions`); `anthropic-messages` → `anthropic_messages`; `openai-codex-responses` → `responses` (allowed **only** for provider `openai-codex`). Any other API name is refused. |
| `providers.<name>.apiKey` | `$VAR` → `api_key_env: VAR`. Values starting with `!` (shell commands) are ignored. Literal keys are copied into `settings.Endpoints[<name>]` (never stored in the catalog layer) unless `settings.yaml` already defines that endpoint. If empty or ignored, poo checks the resolved auth file for an `api_key` entry under `<name>`. |
| `models[].id` | `model_id` (and `<provider>/<id>` catalog name) |
| `models[].input` | `inputs` (validated against `text`, `image`, `audio`) |
| `models[].contextWindow` | `context_limit` |
| `models[].maxTokens` | `max_output` |
| `models[].reasoning` + `models[].compat.supportsReasoningEffort` | When both are `true`, sets `reasoning: { mode: effort, param: reasoning_effort }`. |
| `models[].thinkingLevelMap` | When `reasoning` and `supportsReasoningEffort` are both `true`: non-null keys in canonical order (`off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`) become `reasoning_levels`. If `thinkingLevelMap` is omitted, defaults to `[off, low, medium, high]`. |

## `builtin-models.yaml` and `POO_BUILTIN_MODELS`

poo embeds `config/builtin-models.yaml` in the binary using the exact same `models.yaml` schema. It provides definitions for built-in providers whose endpoints do not expose a full model list or require provider metadata (`session_header`, `skip_probe`, `api`, `reasoning_levels`):

- `openai-codex` (Responses API, `skip_probe: true`)
- `ollama-cloud` (`OLLAMA_API_KEY`)
- `opencode`, `opencode-go`, `opencode-anthropic`, `opencode-go-anthropic` (`OPENCODE_API_KEY`, `session_header: x-opencode-session`)
- `typesafe` (`TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, `skip_probe: true`, `instructions_per_question: true`, `ops: [systemone]`)

### Gating and Precedence

- Built-in providers are added only when a credential file exists at the resolved auth path.
- Each built-in endpoint is gated on its own credential. `openai-codex` requires an `openai-codex` entry in the credential file. Endpoints with `api_key_env` require that key via environment variable, auth file, or a literal in `settings.yaml`.
- Your `models.yaml` or `models.json` folds **over** the built-ins by name, so you can override any built-in endpoint or model without losing the others.

### Overriding with `POO_BUILTIN_MODELS`

Set the `POO_BUILTIN_MODELS` environment variable to a YAML or JSON file path (in the same `models.yaml` schema) to replace the embedded `builtin-models.yaml`:

```bash
POO_BUILTIN_MODELS=/path/to/custom-builtins.yaml poo models
```

When `POO_BUILTIN_MODELS` is set, poo always reads and validates that file even without a credential file. A missing or invalid file fails the load immediately.

---

<!-- Source: reference/manifests.md -->

# Manifests Reference

`poo` loads three external manifest types: **feeds**, **CLI registry** (`cli_registry`), and **MCP servers** (`mcp.json`). All three share a discovery model and XDG default directories, while differing in format support, strictness, and how entries activate.

## Comparison

| Aspect | `feeds` | `cli_registry` | `mcp.json` (+ `poo` block) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Long-lived event sources (`feed:<name>`) | Typed CLI and script tools (`call_cli`) | Stdio MCP servers (`call_mcp`) and MCP resource feeds |
| **Formats** | `.json`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.toml` | `.json`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.toml` | `.json` only (non-`.json` files skipped in dirs; rejected if named directly) |
| **Top-level envelope** | `version: 1`, `feeds: {...}` | `version: 1`, `tools: {...}`, optional `availability` | `mcpServers: {...}`, optional `poo: {...}` |
| **Unknown fields** | Rejected everywhere | Rejected everywhere | Ignored at top level and inside `mcpServers.<name>`; **rejected** inside `poo` |
| **Duplicate keys** | Rejected | Rejected | Rejected everywhere in file |
| **Duplicate names across files** | Load error (names both files) | Load error (names both files) | Load error for duplicate server names or resource feed names |
| **Default XDG directory** | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/poo/feeds/` | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/poo/cli-registry/` | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/poo/mcp/` |
| **Settings keys** | `feeds.paths`, `feeds.defaults` | `cli_registry.paths`, `cli_registry.defaults` | `mcp.paths`, `mcp.defaults` |
| **Profile override** | `profiles.<name>.feeds_defaults` | `profiles.<name>.cli_registry_defaults` | `profiles.<name>.mcp_defaults` |
| **Env var** | `POO_FEEDS_PATH` | `POO_CLI_REGISTRY_PATH` | `POO_MCP_PATH` |
| **CLI flag (repeatable)** | `--feeds-path` | `--cli-registry-path` | `--mcp-path` |
| **Activation** | Always-on feeds start automatically; `optional: true` starts via `subscribe_feed` | Offered on profiles with a side-effecting tool (filtered by `availability`) | Declared only; started only when named in `profiles.<name>.mcp_servers` |

## Discovery and default XDG directories

For each manifest kind, `poo` discovers files from:

1. The default XDG directory (when defaults are enabled):
   - `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/poo/feeds/`
   - `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/poo/cli-registry/`
   - `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/poo/mcp/`
2. Paths listed in `<kind>.paths` in settings.
3. Paths from `POO_FEEDS_PATH`, `POO_CLI_REGISTRY_PATH`, or `POO_MCP_PATH` (OS path-list separated; scrubbed from child processes).
4. Repeatable CLI flags: `--feeds-path`, `--cli-registry-path`, `--mcp-path`.

Discovery rules:

- A missing default XDG directory is ignored, not an error.
- Paths starting with `~/` resolve under the user's home directory. Relative paths resolve against the binary's working directory (where the process starts), not a per-session working directory.
- Every path may be a file or a directory. Discovered files are deduplicated and sorted deterministically.
- Loading is all-or-nothing: a schema error, duplicate name, or missing explicit path fails the build and names the offending file.

## `*.defaults` and profile interaction

Whether a manifest kind's default XDG directory loads is decided by a two-level precedence chain:

1. **`profiles.<name>.<kind>_defaults`** (wins when set; inherited from the profile's `base` if omitted)
2. **`<kind>.defaults`** in top-level settings
3. **Default: `true`** (when neither is set)

```yaml
feeds:
  defaults: false        # off globally

profiles:
  worker:
    base: code
    feeds_defaults: true # re-enabled for this profile and its children
    cli_registry_defaults: false
    mcp_defaults: false
    mcp_servers: [avenor]
```

Two profile lists interact with manifests differently:

- **`profiles.<name>.mcp_servers`** is a **selection**: loading `mcp.json` only declares servers; a session starts only the servers named in its profile's `mcp_servers` (merged with `base`). An unknown server name emits a warning.
- **`profiles.<name>.feeds`** is a **presence assertion**, not a filter. It declares feeds the profile expects to exist, satisfied by either a feed manifest or an active MCP server's resource feed. Missing names emit a warning; loaded feeds still run regardless of this list.

See [Profiles & Prompts](/configuration/profiles-and-prompts) for full profile inheritance rules.

---

## Feed manifests

Top-level envelope:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "feeds": {
    "<name>": {
      "description": "Short summary shown in the jobs prompt.",
      "command": ["my-watcher", "--stream"],
      "env": {
        "API_TOKEN": "env:API_TOKEN",
        "SESSION_ID": "session:id",
        "TARGET_URL": "scope:url",
        "MODE": "watch"
      },
      "restart": true,
      "on_idle": "wake",
      "max_pending": 16,
      "optional": true,
      "scope": {
        "url": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^https://"}
      },
      "filter": {
        "question": "Does this event require action?",
        "min_no_probability": 0.9
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Feed entry fields

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | `string[]` | Yes | Non-empty argv executed by the session's executor. |
| `description` | `string` | No | Description rendered in the jobs prompt. |
| `env` | `map<string, string>` | No | Added on top of benign env vars. Values: literal, `env:NAME` (scrubbed host env), `session:id`, or `scope:NAME` (must match a declared `scope` field). |
| `restart` | `bool` | No | Default `false`. Restart with exponential backoff (`1s` to `60s`, reset after `60s` uptime). Ignored when suspended by a command filter fault. |
| `on_idle` | `"wake" \| "hold"` | No | Whether inputs wake an idle session. Defaults to `jobs.on_idle` (always-on) or `"hold"` (`optional: true`). |
| `max_pending` | `int` (`>= 0`) | No | Maximum queued undelivered inputs before dropping oldest. `0` or omitted uses default `16`. |
| `optional` | `bool` | No | Default `false`. When `true`, starts only via `subscribe_feed`. |
| `scope` | `map<string, ScopeField>` | No | Allowed only when `optional: true`. Keys match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`. Each value has `type: "string"` (required) and optional Go regex `pattern`. |
| `filter` | `Filter` | No | Either `{"question": "...", "min_no_probability": 0.5 < p <= 1}` or `{"command": [...]}`. Never both. |

Validation rules:

- `version` must be `1`.
- Feed names must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$` and cannot collide with another feed manifest or an MCP resource feed.
- A `scope` block on a non-optional feed fails load.
- A `scope:NAME` reference in `env` must name a declared field in `scope`.

For stdout line format, filter runtime behavior, and `subscribe_feed`, see [Feeds & Daemon](/capabilities/feeds-and-daemon).

---

## CLI Registry manifests

CLI registry manifests are loaded by `github.com/sdougbrown/cli-registry` and exposed through `call_cli` (and `find_tool` when a decision model is active and the catalog exceeds 30 entries).

Top-level envelope:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "tools": {
    "<name>": {
      "description": "Wait for a child run to finish.",
      "command": ["avenor", "await", "--until=done", "--format=json"],
      "env": {
        "AVENOR_BIND_HOST": "poo",
        "AVENOR_BIND_SESSION": "session:id"
      },
      "timeout": "36m",
      "inputSchema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "target": {"type": "string", "description": "Child run ID or label."}
        },
        "required": ["target"],
        "additionalProperties": false
      },
      "bindings": [
        {"property": "target", "style": "positional"}
      ],
      "output": {
        "mode": "json",
        "success_exit_codes": [0, 10, 11, 12]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Tool entry fields

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | `string` | Yes | Shown in the catalog prompt and `find_tool` results. |
| `command` | `string[]` | Yes | Base argv executed through the session's executor. |
| `env` | `map<string, string>` | No | Added on top of benign env vars. Supports literals, `env:NAME` (scrubbed host env), and `session:id`. |
| `timeout` | `string` | No | Go duration string (e.g. `"36m"`, `"30s"`) overriding default command timeout. |
| `inputSchema` | `object` | No | JSON Schema validating model arguments before spawning a process. |
| `bindings` | `Binding[]` | No | Maps `inputSchema` properties onto argv or stdin. Each entry names `property`, `style` (`positional`, `equals`, `stdin`, `json`, etc.), and optional `flag`. |
| `output` | `object` | No | `mode`: `"raw"`, `"json"`, or `"json-pointer"`. Optional `success_exit_codes` (`int[]`) treats listed exit codes as non-errors. |

An optional top-level `availability` block may declare Umpire v1 rules over load-time conditions to filter which entries a session offers.

### Non-CLI script (`fn`) tools

A `cli_registry` entry can wrap a script with a pure JSON stdin/stdout contract:

```json
{
  "description": "Sum a pair",
  "command": ["python3", "fn_notes.py"],
  "bindings": [{"property": "data", "style": "json"}],
  "output": {"mode": "json"}
}
```

- `style: "json"` serializes a concrete `object` or `array` schema property to the script's stdin (a tool may have at most one `stdin` or `json` binding; `flag` is optional).
- `output.mode: "json"` returns stdout JSON directly as the tool result (nonzero exit is an error with stderr diagnostics).
- Edge case: a JSON `null` result falls back to the exit-code envelope; wrap nullable results in an object such as `{"result": null}`.

See [CLI Registry & Script Tools](/capabilities/cli-registry) for usage details.

---

## MCP manifests (`mcp.json` + `poo` block)

`mcp.json` uses the standard `mcpServers` format shared with Claude Code and other harnesses, plus an optional top-level `poo` block for resource feeds.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "avenor": {
      "command": "avenor",
      "args": ["mcp", "--bind-host", "poo", "--bind-session", "${session:id}"],
      "env": {
        "AVENOR_LOG": "${AVENOR_LOG:-info}"
      }
    }
  },
  "poo": {
    "servers": {
      "avenor": {
        "feeds": {
          "avenor-inbox": {
            "resource": "avenor://inbox",
            "on_idle": "wake",
            "description": "Messages from Avenor children.",
            "filter": {
              "command": ["jq", "-c", ".text | fromjson | .messages[]"]
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### `mcpServers.<name>` fields

Server names must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` and be unique across all loaded MCP manifests.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | `string` | Yes (for `stdio`) | Executable path or name (template string). |
| `args` | `string[]` | No | Command arguments (template strings). |
| `env` | `map<string, string>` | No | Environment variables (template strings), merged on top of the scrubbed host environment. An explicit `${NAME}` can re-inject a scrubbed variable. |
| `type` | `string` | No | Must be absent or `"stdio"` to launch. `"http"`, `"sse"`, and `"streamable-http"` are skipped with a warning; any other value fails load. |
| `url` | `string` | No | If set with no `type`, treated as `"http"` and skipped with a warning. |

Unknown top-level keys and unknown fields inside an `mcpServers` entry are ignored so one `mcp.json` works across harnesses.

### Launch-time templates

`command`, each element of `args`, and each value in `env` are parsed at load time and resolved when the server launches for a session:

| Syntax | Resolution |
|---|---|
| `${NAME}` | Host environment variable `NAME`. Launch fails if unset. |
| `${NAME:-default}` | Host environment variable `NAME`, or `default` if unset. |
| `${session:id}` | The session's native ID (preserved across resumes). |
| `$$` | Literal `$`. |

Load-time errors: unterminated `${`, empty variable name, a `:-default` on `${session:...}`, or any `session:` key other than `id`.

### The `poo` block

The top-level `poo` key is owned strictly by `poo`: any unknown field inside `poo` fails load.

Path: `poo.servers.<server>.feeds.<feed>`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `resource` | `string` | Yes | MCP resource URI to subscribe to. Unique per server. |
| `description` | `string` | No | Description rendered in the jobs prompt. |
| `on_idle` | `"wake" \| "hold"` | No | Idle delivery policy; inherits `jobs.on_idle` when omitted. |
| `filter` | `Filter` | No | Same `command` or `question` filter schema as [Feed manifests](#feed-manifests). |

Validation rules:

- `<server>` must be defined in the same file's `mcpServers` and use the `stdio` transport.
- `<feed>` must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$` and be unique across all MCP resource feeds and all loaded `feeds` manifests.
- Two feeds on the same server cannot subscribe to the same `resource` URI.

See [MCP Servers](/capabilities/mcp-servers) for startup timeouts, relaunch budgets, and `call_mcp`.

---

<!-- Source: reference/session-log-v0.md -->

# Session log v0

A poo session log is an append-only JSONL file: one JSON object per line,
in the order the records were produced. This document is the contract a
consumer parses.

A session log holds one session. The file is created exclusively, so a run
pointed at a log that already exists fails before it sends a request rather
than appending a second session to the log.

## Where a session's log lives

A logged session's log is `<dir>/<session_id>.jsonl`, and its lock is
`<dir>/<session_id>.lock`. The lock is an exclusive `flock`, taken when the
session is created or loaded and held until the session is closed: a second
process is refused while the session is live, and the kernel releases the
lock when the holding process dies. The lock file is never deleted, and a
lock file with no log beside it is a harmless leftover.

The log is built in a temporary file and renamed into place, so a session
that was cut short during its construction is never a session: the
temporary file is left behind, and a prune removes it once it is old.

A log that was cut short in the middle of a record is truncated when the
session is loaded: the bytes after the last newline are not a record. The
load then recovers the session, appending the records that resolve what
the session left open: an `interrupted` result, and the message that
carries it, for every tool call without one, a denied
`permission.answered` for every ask without an answer, a `run.settled`
with the reason `interrupted` for every run that never settled, a
`job.ended` with the outcome `interrupted` for every job that never
ended, a `feed.ended` with the outcome `interrupted` for every feed
attempt that never ended, an `input.delivered` for every input whose
`message` names it in `input_id` but has no `input.delivered` after it, and
an `input.dropped` with the reason `interrupted` for every input that
never reached the model. The recovery
appends only what is missing, so loading a session twice writes nothing
twice.

A delivery write that outlives the finalization's wait is a stalled
store. The finalization gives a delivery's message and fate their own
record budgets before that decision, so a delivery within both budgets
is not a stall; the wait remains bounded at two record budgets. When the
store does stall, the session breaks, the store failure is the run's
reason (or a losing candidate when the run was cancelled), and the
input's fate is left to the records that land and to a load, which
applies the two rules above.

The finalization and the close each attempt a bounded flush. A store
that is still stalled at the bound is reported by the close's
`ErrCloseStalled`; records it has not stored or flushed cannot be
recovered, so a load applies the rules above only to what the store
holds.

The first record is always `session.created`, and it carries
`"format": "poo-session-v0"`. A consumer that does not recognise the format
should stop rather than guess.

## Common fields

Every record carries these three fields, from the same envelope:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `record` | string | The record's name, e.g. `"tool.call"`. |
| `seq` | integer | The session-monotonic sequence number. The first record is 1. |
| `ts` | string | The record's timestamp, RFC 3339 with nanosecond precision, in UTC. |

The record's own fields follow the envelope.

A record that someone produced also carries an `origin`:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `origin` | string | Who produced the record: `"user"`, `"model"`, `"tool"`, `"system"`, `"job"`, `"steer"`, `"interrupt"`, `"follow_up"`, `"compaction"`, `"feed:<name>"`, `"feed:<name>[<field>=<value>]"` or `"hook:<name>"`. **Absent** on the records that no one produced: the session's own header, a run's boundaries, the usage accounting. |

## Record names

| Name | Written when |
|---|---|
| `session.created` | Once, first, when the session starts. |
| `run.started` | Once per run, when the run begins. |
| `system_prompt` | Once per run whose prompt differs from the previous one, with the whole prompt. |
| `message` | Once per message that enters the model's history. |
| `tool.call` | Once per tool call the model makes, before it runs. A call a running tool made through the nested seam is recorded here too, with the parent call's handle in `parent`. |
| `tool.result` | Once per tool call, after it runs. |
| `usage` | Once per provider request. |
| `provider.attempt` | Once per attempt of a request that failed. |
| `input.queued` | Once per input the session accepts. |
| `input.delivered` | Once per input that reaches the model. It follows the `message` that delivers the input, and that message names the input in `input_id`. |
| `input.dropped` | Once per input that never reaches the model. |
| `input.held` | Once per round of job results that were held instead of delivered. |
| `job.started` | Once per background job, when it is accepted. |
| `job.ended` | Once per background job, when it finishes. |
| `feed.started` | Once per attempt of a feed, when the attempt starts. |
| `feed.ended` | Once per attempt of a feed, when the attempt ends. |
| `tool.started` | Once per side-effecting tool call, when the call starts. |
| `run.resumed` | Once per run that resumes after a crash. |
| `turn.hook` | Once per turn hook, at its start and at its end. |
| `feed.subscribed` | Once per feed instance, when it subscribes, and again when a call changes the prompt it screens its records with. |
| `feed.unsubscribed` | Once per feed instance, when it unsubscribes. |
| `observer.dropped` | Once a second at most, per observer that fell behind. |
| `turn.interrupted` | Once per turn an interrupt cut short. |
| `compaction` | Once per compaction a compactor produced. |
| `session.models_changed` | Once per model switch, between the runs. |
| `model.output_limit` | Once per learned output cap, when an endpoint rejects a request's `max_tokens`. |
| `decision` | Once per decision call, failures included. |
| `permission.asked` | Once per permission ask, when the run starts waiting for an answer. |
| `permission.answered` | Once per permission ask, when the answer arrives. |
| `run.settled` | Once per run, when the run ends. |

The fields of the records grow over time. A consumer must tolerate a field
it does not recognise: the fields below are the ones the current core
writes, and a later stage adds more.

## `session.created`

The first record of a log.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `format` | string | The record vocabulary. Always `"poo-session-v0"`. |
| `session_id` | string | The session's identifier. |
| `mode` | string | The persistence mode. `"logged"` for a `poo run`. |
| `created_at` | string | RFC 3339, UTC. |
| `working_dir` | string | The absolute directory the run works in. |
| `profile` | string | The profile the session was built from. Absent when the log was written before the field existed. |
| `roles` | object | The models the session talked to. See below. |
| `model` | object | The model the session talks to. See below. |
| `tools` | array of objects | The tools linked into the session, in call order. |
| `settings_hash` | string | The hash of the settings the session was built with. Absent when the log was written before the field existed. |
| `context_limit` | integer | The model's context window, in tokens. |
| `tools_mode` | string | How the run asks for tool calls: `"native"`, `"text"` or `"auto"`. |
| `reasoning_effort` | string | The `reasoning_effort` the run sends. Absent when it sends none. |
| `build` | object | The binary that produced the session. |

`roles` holds the session's effective roles:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `chat` | object | The chat model. Absent when the session had none. |
| `decider` | object | The decision model. Absent when the session had none. |

A role holds model info: its `name`, its `model_id`, its `endpoint`,
its `api`, its `ops`, its `context_limit` and its `input_limit`. The roles
are the ones the session ran with, not the ones the current settings would
pick: a session loaded by another binary keeps the roles it was made with.

`context_limit` is the whole window the prompt and the answer share, and
`input_limit` is the largest prompt the endpoint accepts, absent when it
takes its whole window. The prompt is bounded by the smaller of the two,
so a consumer that measures a prompt reads both.

`model` holds:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | The provider's model identifier. |
| `endpoint` | string | The endpoint, without credentials. Absent when empty. Renamed from `base_url` before v1; older logs carry `base_url`. |
| `max_output` | integer | The model's output-token limit. Absent when unknown. |

The `endpoint` never carries credentials: a URL that names a user and a
password is written without its userinfo, so a consumer can read the log
without picking up a secret.

Each entry of `tools` holds:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | The tool's identifier. |
| `class` | string | The tool's side-effect class: `"read_only"` or `"side_effecting"`. |
| `background` | string | The tool's background mode: `"allowed"` or `"always"`. Absent when the tool never runs in the background. |
| `idempotent` | boolean | `true` for a `"side_effecting"` tool whose repeated execution is safe, so a durable session may replay an interrupted call. Absent when the tool does not declare it, and on a log written before the field existed. |

`build` holds:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | The binary's name. |
| `version` | string | The binary's version. |

## `run.started`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | string | The run's identifier: a ULID (26 characters of Crockford base32, the time first). |
| `prompt_hash` | string | The hex SHA-256 of the prompt text. |
| `started_at` | string | RFC 3339, UTC. |
| `model_id` | string | The model the run talks to. |
| `max_turns` | integer | The turn limit. `0` means the run is unlimited. |
| `tools_mode` | string | How the run asks for tool calls. |
| `reasoning_effort` | string | The `reasoning_effort` the run sends. Absent when it sends none. |
| `trigger` | string | What started the run: `"prompt"`, `"job"` or `"feed"`. Absent on a log written before the field existed. |
| `jobs` | array of objects | The job results that started a job run. Absent on a prompt run. |
| `feeds` | array of strings | The feed instances whose inputs started the run, by label (`feed.started` names the form), in queue order. Absent when no feed's input started the run. A wake that carried both a job's result and a feed's input has the trigger `"job"` and names the feeds too. |

A `jobs` entry holds:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `job` | string | The job's identifier, e.g. `"j3"`. |
| `handle` | string | The handle of the tool call the job came from, e.g. `"r1"`. The call returned at once with a `started` outcome, and the job carries that call's handle. |
| `tool` | string | The tool the job ran. |
| `text` | string | The job's result, as the model reads it. |
| `outcome` | string | The job's outcome. |

## `message`

One message in the model's history. The messages in the log are the same
list the model sees: nothing is trimmed, rewritten or summarised.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | string | The run the message belongs to. |
| `turn` | integer | The turn the message belongs to. `0` for the run's input. |
| `origin` | string | Who produced the message: `"user"`, `"model"`, `"tool"`, `"system"`, `"job"`, `"steer"`, `"interrupt"`, `"follow_up"`, `"compaction"`, `"feed:<name>"`, `"feed:<name>[<field>=<value>]"` or `"hook:<name>"`. |
| `role` | string | The message's role: `"system"`, `"user"`, `"assistant"` or `"tool"`. |
| `content` | array of objects | The message's content blocks. |
| `message_id` | string | The message's session-monotonic id, e.g. `"m7"`. Absent when the message has none. |
| `input_id` | string | The input delivered by this message. Absent on other messages and older logs. |
| `partial` | boolean | `true` when the message was cut short. Absent when it was not. |
| `cause` | string | Why the message was cut short: `"interrupt"` or `"provider_error"`. Absent unless the message is partial. |
| `delivery_note` | object | How much of the previous reply the user had seen. Absent when the message carries none. |
| `data` | object | The object a feed's filter wrote beside the message's text: the structured record. Absent unless a filter produced one. |

A partial message is the text a cut-short response carried. The
assistant's own tool calls in a partial response did not run, and the
calls that did not run are recorded as `skipped`.

`delivery_note` holds:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `message_id` | string | The assistant message the user had seen part of. |
| `upto_chars` | integer | How many characters of that message the user had seen, in code points over its text blocks. |
| `text` | string | The rendered note. It is prefixed to the text of the message, followed by a blank line, so the message's `content` holds it too. Empty when the whole reply was presented. |

The note is part of the record, so a replay shows exactly what the user
saw. The assistant message itself is never trimmed: the note is the
record.

Each content block holds:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | `"text"`, `"thinking"`, `"tool_call"`, `"tool_result"`, `"image"` or `"provider"`. |
| `text` | string | The block's text. Absent when empty. |
| `tool_call_id` | string | The provider's id for the call. Set on `tool_call` and `tool_result` blocks. |
| `name` | string | The tool's name. Set on `tool_call` and `tool_result` blocks. |
| `arguments` | object or string | A `tool_call` block's arguments. A JSON object when the model sent valid JSON, and a JSON string holding the raw text when it did not. |
| `is_error` | boolean | `true` when a `tool_result` reports a failure. Absent when false. |
| `media_type` | string | An attachment block's media type, e.g. `"image/png"`. |
| `data` | string | An attachment block's bytes, base64-encoded. |
| `provider` | object | The block's opaque provider companion. Absent when the block has none. |

A `tool_result` block's `text` is the model-facing text of the result.

A `provider` block holds:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `api` | string | The wire API the payload belongs to: `"chat_completions"`, `"responses"` or `"anthropic_messages"`. |
| `type` | string | The provider's own name for the payload, e.g. `"thinking_signature"`, `"reasoning"`, `"redacted_thinking"` or `"compaction"`. |
| `data` | any | The payload, verbatim. The core never interprets it. |
| `required` | boolean | `true` when a request cannot be made without the payload. Absent when false. |

A `provider` payload may also ride as the `provider` field of a `thinking`
block: an Anthropic thinking block is one block on the wire, with a text
part and a signature, and poo keeps the two together.

## `system_prompt`

The prompt a run rendered, whole. A prompt that differs from the previous
one is written; an unchanged one is not. The record is what a restored
session takes: the prompt is never rendered from the sections again, so a
session that was recorded under another prompt keeps that prompt.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | string | The run the prompt belongs to. |
| `variant` | string | The variant the prompt rendered in. Absent when it rendered in the default one. |
| `text` | string | The whole rendered prompt. |
| `hash` | string | The hex SHA-256 of the text. |

## `tool.call`

A tool call the model made. The record is written before the tool runs, so
a log shows what the model asked for even when the tool never finished.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | string | The run the call belongs to. |
| `turn` | integer | The turn the call belongs to. |
| `handle` | string | The call's handle within the turn, e.g. `"r1"`. |
| `tool` | string | The tool the model called. |
